reconstruction: The source and target letters are normalized; the substantive simplex condition is unchanged. Pairwise adjacency of images alone is insufficient for contiguity unless the target is flag, and the target in this talk is not flag in general.
fate: \citet[\S\S7--10, especially \S9, Remark~(b)]{vaserstein1976foundations} formalizes this standard simplicial notion before applying it to the five-block argument.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard contiguity, with the required whole-simplex condition preserved.

title: Interleaved block sum and its homotopy invariance
notes: The injections \(f(i)=2i\), \(g(i)=2i+1\) give \(a\oplus b=a^f+b^g\). The raw operation is described as noncommutative, nonassociative, and without a neutral element; it induces \(SA\times SA\to SA\).
statement: Disjoint coordinate embeddings define a block-sum map on finite matrices and on the simplicial spaces. Different choices of embeddings, parenthesization, and order are related on homotopy groups by stabilization homotopies. Consequently the operation on classes has a neutral element and is independent of those choices, even though the chosen coordinate formula is not strictly associative or strictly unital.
reconstruction: The product is the simplicial product appropriate to the model, and the claim about operations on all \(K_i\), \(i\geq0\), exceeds the displayed definition when \(i=0\); here the conclusion is restricted to \(i\geq1\). A separately defined \(K_0\) also has direct sum, but is not constructed on these pages.
fate: The exact framework appears in \citet{vaserstein1973foundations}, received on 14 November 1972, the day after this talk; the detailed treatment \citet{vaserstein1976foundations} was received on 26 February 1975 and published in 1976. See \citet[\S4 and Corollary~13.1]{vaserstein1976foundations}. The basic block-sum idea is older; the source supplies the precise coordinate and homotopy bookkeeping.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established block-sum operation in positive K theory; the isolated zero index is annotated.

title: Interchange gives abelian group structures
notes: Block sum and the previously introduced homotopy operations are mutually distributive, hence coincide and are commutative. The page describes the resulting sum as an H-space structure.
statement: Under the unital hypothesis, block sum induces abelian group laws on all \(K_n(A)\), \(n\geq1\), agreeing with ordinary homotopy-group composition where that already exists. The key algebraic principle is the interchange law for two binary operations with the same two-sided identity: the operations then agree and are associative and commutative. A homotopy-unit H-space formulation expresses the same block-sum construction on realization.
reconstruction: For \(K_1=\pi_0\), inverses and a group operation must be supplied rather than inferred solely from the topology of components; the ensuing elementary quotient provides them. The word distributive is interpreted as the interchange identity, not the ordinary ring distributive law.
fate: \citet[Lemma~10.2, Corollary~13.1, and Theorem~13.2]{vaserstein1976foundations} proves exactly these assertions. The interchange principle and the already-known K-group structures are expository; no new general H-space theorem is attributed to the talk.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard abelian positive K groups, with the low-degree group-law issue accounted for.

title: Infinite block sum and vanishing of cone K theory
notes: On \(\widetilde\Omega A\) even an infinite number of matrices can be summed in blocks; the notes conclude that its K functors are trivial.
statement: For an associative unital ring \(A\), the row-and-column-finite cone ring admits an infinite-sum endomorphism compatible with two complementary coordinate embeddings. On positive K groups its identity satisfies \(x+\rho_*(x)=\rho_*(x)\); hence \(K_n(\widetilde\Omega A)=0\) for \(n\geq1\). Infinite sums mean a specified block-diagonal placement with finite support in each row and column, not arbitrary entrywise infinite sums.
reconstruction: The unital hypothesis introduced on P000469 is retained. Extending the vanishing to \(K_0\) and negative degrees requires the separately developed theory; none is defined by the homotopy formula in this talk. This is the algebraic Eilenberg swindle in the specified matrix model.
fate: The exact framework appears in \citet{vaserstein1973foundations}, received on 14 November 1972, the day after this talk; the detailed treatment \citet{vaserstein1976foundations} was received on 26 February 1975 and published in 1976. The first theorem of the 1973 announcement states cone vanishing; \citet[Lemmas~18.1--18.2 and Corollary~18.1]{vaserstein1976foundations} gives the infinite-sum proof. Earlier occurrences are 1971-253.5 and 1971-256.3; A records the subsequent implementation, not a new origin for the swindle.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: published cone-vanishing theorem with an exact infinite-sum construction; no unresolved cone problem here.

title: K one as components modulo elementary matrices
notes: \(K_1A=\pi_0SA\); \(EA\) is the identity component, described as products of elementary or pseudotriangular matrices.
statement: For unital \(A\), the component of the identity vertex in \(SA\) consists of the stable elementary subgroup \(E(A)\subset\mathrm{GL}(A)\). Thus \(\pi_0SA\cong\mathrm{GL}(A)/E(A)=K_1(A)\). A path consists of finitely many simplex edges, and triangular factors decompose into elementary transvections.
reconstruction: Component is understood in the realization or in edge-path connectivity, rather than in a topology on the discrete set of matrices. The ordinary multiplicative elementary matrix is \(I+aE_{ij}\), corresponding to \(aE_{ij}\) in circle coordinates.
fate: The classical quotient predates the talk; \citet[III, Whitehead's Lemma~1.3.3]{weibel2013kbook} records it and its 1950 antecedent. The exact component computation is \citet[Theorems~14.1--14.2]{vaserstein1976foundations}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard K-one identification; no new quotient conjecture.

title: Elementary perfectness and the idempotent-ring extension
notes: The notes explicitly allow either \(A\ni1\) or \(AA=A\), then assert \(EA=[GMA,GMA]=[EA,EA]\).
statement: If \(A\) is an associative ring satisfying \(A^2=A\), where \(A^2\) is the additive subgroup generated by products, then the stable elementary group satisfies \(E(A)=[GMA,GMA]=[E(A),E(A)]\). In particular it is perfect, and the stable quasiunit abelianization is the elementary quotient. A unital ring satisfies the idempotence condition automatically.
reconstruction: The idempotent condition means finite sums of products, not that every element is a single product. It applies here to the commutator assertion; no blanket extension of every subsequent universal-central-extension claim to all nonunital idempotent rings is inferred.
fate: The exact framework appears in \citet{vaserstein1973foundations}, received on 14 November 1972, the day after this talk; the detailed treatment \citet{vaserstein1976foundations} was received on 26 February 1975 and published in 1976. \citet[Theorem~5.1, pp.~103--104]{vaserstein1976foundations}, applied with \(B=A\), proves the nonunital idempotent extension. The unital Whitehead theorem is older; class A concerns the stated extension and its publication in the speaker's treatment.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: published under the precise idempotent-ring hypothesis.

title: Triangular generators and their elementary relations
notes: \(\Theta A\) is said to have generators \(a^{ij}\), with \(a\) in position \((i,j)\), the addition relation, the adjacent-root commutator relation, and commuting relations for some other pairs.
statement: For a fixed coordinate order, the unitriangular group is generated by \(t_{ij}(a)=I+aE_{ij}\), \(i\prec j\), with \(t_{ij}(a)t_{ij}(b)=t_{ij}(a+b)\), \([t_{ij}(a),t_{jk}(b)]=t_{ik}(ab)\) for \(i\prec j\prec k\), and \([t_{ij}(a),t_{kl}(b)]=1\) when \(j\ne k\) and \(i\ne l\). In the stable finite-support setting these are the triangular presentation relations.
reconstruction: The allowed indices and the omitted commuting condition are reconstructed explicitly. The presentation of a fixed triangular group is distinguished from the all-root Steinberg presentation and from a presentation of \(E(A)\), which generally has additional K-two relations.
fate: \citet[\S6 and the triangular map in the proof of Theorem~15.2]{vaserstein1976foundations} uses these relations to pass from triangular groups to the Steinberg group. The general relations are also stated in \citet[III, \S5.1]{weibel2013kbook}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard triangular elementary relations; the notebook's phrase defining relations is correct only with its group and index set specified.

title: Stable Steinberg group with the missing index restrictions restored
notes: The group \(\operatorname{St}A\) is generated by all the displayed elementary symbols and Steinberg relations; the commuting cases are abbreviated as some commutators being zero.
statement:
For an associative ring \(A\), define \(\operatorname{St}(A)\) on generators \(x_{ij}(a)\), \(i
e j\), with \(x_{ij}(a)x_{ij}(b)=x_{ij}(a+b)\), \([x_{ij}(a),x_{jk}(b)]=x_{ik}(ab)\) for distinct \(i,j,k\), and \([x_{ij}(a),x_{kl}(b)]=1\) if \(i
e l\) and \(j
e k\). It maps onto \(E(A)\) by \(x_{ij}(a)\mapsto I+aE_{ij}\).
reconstruction: Zero in the notes is the identity of the circle-law convention; the abstract group relations use one. The full index restrictions are essential. Opposite-root pairs are not declared commuting.
fate: This is the classical Steinberg construction, treated before the talk in \citet{milnor1972introduction} (publisher date 21 January 1972). The precise presentation was read in \citet[III, Definition~5.1]{weibel2013kbook} and \citet[\S6]{vaserstein1976foundations}; the Milnor publisher page alone is used for chronology, not as a claim to have read its theorem text.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established stable Steinberg presentation.

title: Steinberg group as paths and the K two kernel
notes: Loops represent relations among elementary matrices; the exact sequence \(0\to K_2A\to\operatorname{St}A\to EA\to0\) is displayed. Steinberg-group elements are described as homotopy classes of paths starting at zero with endpoints fixed under homotopy.
statement: For a unital ring, the path-group model of \(\operatorname{St}(A)\) maps a based path class to its endpoint in \(E(A)\), with multiplication using translated concatenation. Its kernel is the loop group \(\pi_1(SA,I)=K_2(A)\); thus \(1\to K_2(A)\to\operatorname{St}(A)\to E(A)\to1\) is exact.
reconstruction: The group law on paths is not bare concatenation of paths with unrelated endpoints; translation makes the endpoints composable. The zeroes in the group exact sequence are conventional shorthand and are rewritten as ones.
fate: \citet[Theorem~15.2 and Corollary~15.2]{vaserstein1976foundations} proves the exact path/Steinberg identification and attributes the theorem to Volodin. The underlying simplicial theory had circulated by the July 1970 submission of \citet{volodin1971extraordinary}, published in 1971, so the identification is expository here.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the standard positive-degree low-dimensional identification; no new universal-relation problem is posed on these pages.

title: Universal central extension and the second homology of E A
notes: The notes write \(K_2A=H_2EA\) and describe \(\operatorname{St}A\) as the universal central extension of \(EA\).
statement: For an associative unital ring \(A\), the stable Steinberg group \(\operatorname{St}(A)\to E(A)\) is the universal central extension of the perfect elementary group. Therefore \(K_2(A)\cong H_2(E(A);\mathbb Z)\). Stability and the unit convention are part of the assertion; arbitrary small finite matrix ranks require separate results.
reconstruction: The integral trivial coefficients in group homology are supplied. The active unital hypothesis from P000469 is retained, and the immediately preceding idempotent-ring alternative is not automatically propagated to this stronger claim.
fate: The classical Kervaire--Steinberg theorem is stated and proved in \citet[III, Theorem~5.5]{weibel2013kbook}; its preceding discussion points to \citet[\S5]{milnor1972introduction}, published before this talk. The latter's publication was checked from the publisher, while the mathematical theorem was read in Weibel.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established stable unital theorem, with scope distinct from finite-rank or unrestricted nonunital variants.

title: Pairwise simplices need not form a simplex: the tolerance assertion
notes: The explicit \ru{Задача} asks whether three vertices with all three edges present form a simplex, and generalizes this to every finite pairwise adjacent set, calling it a tolerance-space property.
statement: For the complex defined in 1972-280.7, the proposed assertion is: every finite \(X\subset\mathrm{GL}(A)\) whose two-element subsets are simplices is itself a simplex. It is false for every nonzero unital ring. The vertices \(I+E_{12},I+E_{23},I+E_{31}\) are pairwise adjacent but do not lie in any common coset of a permutation-unitriangular subgroup, even after stabilization.
reconstruction: The question is interpreted with the single common translation and order of P000468, not as a flag completion imposed by definition. The complete counterexample, the acyclic-support criterion, and minimal-rank check are proved in the corrective appendix and marked \ours; finite computations are marked \oursComputed. No novelty or priority claim is made for the counterexample.
fate: The exact framework appears in \citet{vaserstein1973foundations}, received on 14 November 1972, the day after this talk; the detailed treatment \citet{vaserstein1976foundations} was received on 26 February 1975 and published in 1976. Crucially, \citet[\S11, Remark~(c), p.~111]{vaserstein1976foundations} asserts exactly this property after defining the complex and identifying left/right conventions in Remark~(b). Thus A records exact publication of the assertion, not its validity. It is not an orphan D item. The same remark says the assertion is not used in that paper, so this correction alone does not refute the paper's K-theory comparisons.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: refuted in the literal model by the fully checked three-vertex example; the published claim is corrected, and no open problem is manufactured from it.

title: Homotopy category of complexes in an abelian category
notes: For an abelian category \(C\), the notes introduce \(K_C\) as the category of complexes and then explicitly specify homotopy classes of complex morphisms as its arrows.
statement: Let \(C\) be an abelian category, with an appropriate smallness convention. The category \(K(C)\) has cochain complexes as objects and chain maps modulo chain homotopy as morphisms. Composition is induced by composition of chain maps. Homology or cohomology is well defined on these morphism classes.
reconstruction: The full sentence defines the homotopy category, not the unquotiented category of complexes. Cochain indexing is chosen for clarity; the notebook's upward arrows can equally be reindexed homologically.
fate: The notes explicitly refer to \citet[Chapter~I, pp.~19--84]{hartshorne1966residues}, published in 1966 from the Harvard seminar of 1963--1964. The publisher record and contents were checked; the exact modern statements and proofs were read separately in \citet[Tags 05R1 and 05RR]{stacks2026foundations}. This is exposition of an established construction, not a 1972 announcement. See also the opening paragraph of Stacks Tag 05RR.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard homotopy-category definition; no ambiguity remains after reading the morphism line.

title: Quasi-isomorphisms as the class to be inverted
notes: The class \(S\subset\operatorname{Hom}K_C\) consists of morphisms inducing isomorphisms on homology.
statement: A morphism in \(K(C)\) is a quasi-isomorphism if its maps \(H^n\) are isomorphisms for every integer \(n\). This condition is invariant under chain homotopy; equivalently the cone of a representing chain map is acyclic. These morphisms form the saturated multiplicative system used in the derived category.
reconstruction: The all-degrees quantifier and cone characterization unpack the abbreviated homology condition. Saturation is a standard structural theorem used for the subsequent localization, not an extra claim that the notes explicitly proved.
fate: The notes explicitly refer to \citet[Chapter~I, pp.~19--84]{hartshorne1966residues}, published in 1966 from the Harvard seminar of 1963--1964. The publisher record and contents were checked; the exact modern statements and proofs were read separately in \citet[Tags 05R1 and 05RR]{stacks2026foundations}. This is exposition of an established construction, not a 1972 announcement. The exact multiplicative-system statement is Stacks Lemma~13.11.2, Tag 05RR.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard quasi-isomorphisms and their localization class.

title: Equivalent left and right cancellation by quasi-isomorphisms
notes: For \(f,g:K\to K'\), the page asserts equivalence between \(fs_1=gs_1\) for a quasi-isomorphism \(s_1:K_1\to K\) and \(s_2f=s_2g\) for a quasi-isomorphism \(s_2:K'\to K_2\).
statement: In the homotopy category of complexes of an abelian category, the following are equivalent for parallel arrows \(f,g:X\to Y\): there exists a quasi-isomorphism \(s:Z\to X\) with \(fs=gs\); there exists a quasi-isomorphism \(t:Y\to W\) with \(tf=tg\); and the images of \(f,g\) in \(D(C)\) agree. All displayed equalities before localization are in \(K(C)\), hence mean chain homotopy for representing maps.
reconstruction: The target arrow's direction is fixed by the scanned diagram. Requiring literal equality of representing chain maps would change the statement; the preceding definition of \(K_C\) is therefore decisive. The equality-in-localization characterization is its standard consequence.
fate: The notes explicitly refer to \citet[Chapter~I, pp.~19--84]{hartshorne1966residues}, published in 1966 from the Harvard seminar of 1963--1964. The publisher record and contents were checked; the exact modern statements and proofs were read separately in \citet[Tags 05R1 and 05RR]{stacks2026foundations}. This is exposition of an established construction, not a 1972 announcement. Stacks Lemma~13.5.5, Tag 05R1, proves both cancellation directions by an acyclic mapping cone and the dual argument.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: a proved calculus-of-fractions lemma; no extra injective or projective resolution hypothesis is needed.

title: Derived localization and composition of fractions
notes: The notes write \(L_C=S^{-1}K_C\), say that the arrows of \(S\) become invertible, and invoke the preceding lemma in defining composition; the reading reference is Hartshorne.
statement: For a small abelian category \(C\), or another setting in which the relevant localization has set-valued Hom classes, define \(D(C)=S^{-1}K(C)\). It is characterized by the universal property that functors from \(K(C)\) inverting all quasi-isomorphisms factor through it. Morphisms may be represented by roofs \(X\xleftarrow{s}Z\xrightarrow{f}Y\), with \(s\in S\); the left/right Ore and cancellation conditions define composition and equality of roofs.
reconstruction: The single displayed cancellation lemma is part of a full calculus of fractions; it alone does not prove every localization axiom. The set-theoretic qualification avoids asserting that every large abelian category has a locally small unbounded derived category. Neither boundedness nor enough injectives is imposed by these particular notes.
fate: The notes explicitly refer to \citet[Chapter~I, pp.~19--84]{hartshorne1966residues}, published in 1966 from the Harvard seminar of 1963--1964. The publisher record and contents were checked; the exact modern statements and proofs were read separately in \citet[Tags 05R1 and 05RR]{stacks2026foundations}. This is exposition of an established construction, not a 1972 announcement. Stacks Definition~13.11.3 gives the localization, and Remark~13.11.4 states the smallness issue explicitly.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the standard derived category in the stated size setting, with the notebook's shorthand expanded.

title: Graded algebra cohomology
notes: For \(A=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}A_n\), the notes augment to \(A_0\), choose a graded free resolution \(C_\bullet\to A_0\), and put \(H^s(A)=\ker d_{s+1}^*/\operatorname{im}d_s^*\).
statement: For a nonnegatively graded augmented algebra over \(A_0\), define \(\operatorname{Ext}_A^{s,t}(A_0,A_0)\) using a graded projective or free resolution; \(s\) is resolution degree and \(t\) records internal degree. The augmentation is projection to degree zero, and \(A_0\) is made an \(A\)-module through it.
fate: Classical derived-functor definition; the notebook cites \citet{cartaneilenberg1956homological,maclane1963homology}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; this is algebra-module Ext, as appropriate after dualizing the earlier coalgebra.

title: Existence of resolutions and independence of the answer
notes: The two stated assertions are that a free resolution exists and that \(H^s(A)\) is independent of the chosen resolution.
statement: Every graded module over a graded ring has a graded free resolution. Comparison maps lifting the identity are unique up to chain homotopy; applying graded \(\operatorname{Hom}\) therefore yields canonically isomorphic Ext groups for any two projective resolutions.
reconstruction: This general theorem does not automatically make the particular relative bar resolution free: its terms also require freeness of the reduced algebra over the base, or a suitable projective/relative version.
fate: Established comparison theorem; \citet[Ch.III]{maclane1963homology}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved well before the lecture.

title: Yoneda multiplication by lifting cocycles
notes: A representative \(C_i\to A_0\) is lifted to maps between the resolutions, and composition with a representative \(C_j\to A_0\) yields \(C_{i+j}\to A_0\).
statement: Lift a cocycle of cohomological degree \(i\) to a degree-\(i\) chain map of the resolution, then compose with a degree-\(j\) cocycle. The resulting degree-\(i+j\) class is independent of lifts and representatives and defines the associative Yoneda product, with the order fixed by this composition convention.
reconstruction: The dashed arrows in the scan are chain-map lifts, not canonical maps on the individual free modules. The diagram's existence uses projectivity and exactness.
fate: Classical Yoneda product; \citet[Ch.XII]{maclane1963homology}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Ext need not be graded commutative
notes: \(H(A)\) is said to be noncommutative ``in a genuine sense'', even though the starting algebra is commutative; a parenthesis contrasts Hopf-algebra examples in topology.
statement: The Yoneda algebra of the augmentation module of a commutative algebra need not obey the graded commutativity rule. For example, if \(A=k\oplus V\) with \(V^2=0\), \(2\le\dim_kV<\infty\), then its normalized bar-cochain differential vanishes and \(\operatorname{Ext}_A(k,k)\cong T(V^*)\). Additional Hopf and symmetry structure is required for standard graded commutativity theorems.
reconstruction: \ours\ The square-zero example follows directly from the next bar differential: every product of two reduced elements vanishes, while concatenation remains free. It gives a precise counterexample; the claim that topology has only commutative rings is read as a comment on the examples under discussion, not as a universal assertion about topology.
fate: Buchstaber's later construction explicitly uses a noncommutative cohomology Hopf algebra: \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the algebraic warning is correct; the historical aside should not be promoted to a general theorem.

title: Homological classification of multivalued formal groups
notes: The single sentence says that classification of multivalued groups rests on the preceding noncommutative cohomology ring.
statement: The notes announce a method: use bar-construction cohomology and its noncommutative product to impose associativity and extension conditions for multivalued formal laws. No number of values, complete axioms, coefficient hypotheses, or classification theorem is stated here.
reconstruction: The later two-valued theory supplies a documented continuation, not missing hypotheses to be retroactively inserted into the notebook. In the 1976 paper the ground ring excludes elements of order two; its first-type computation and second-type reduced-base theorem are more specific results than this sentence.
fate: The method is explicitly outlined in \citet[\S~IV, p.~174]{buchstaber1973classification}, received on 3 January 1973; the detailed realization appears in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}, received 28 April 1975. The exact all-multivalued classification cannot be claimed from these sources.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the announced method has a published two-valued realization; the notebook does not formulate a larger open problem.

title: Normalized bar resolution and its signs
notes: With \(\bar A=\bigoplus_{n>0}A_n\), \(C_s=A\otimes_{A_0}\bar A^{\otimes s}\), and the differential merges adjacent entries. The corrected line says the sign exponent is the position when every element is even.
statement: Over a field, or when the reduced pieces are suitably projective over the base, the augmented normalized bar resolution computes Ext. In the all-even internal-degree case, \(d(a_0[a_1|\cdots|a_s])=a_0a_1[a_2|\cdots|a_s]+\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}(-1)^ja_0[a_1|\cdots|a_ja_{j+1}|\cdots|a_s]\). In a suspended graded convention the remaining signs obey the Koszul rule.
reconstruction: The notebook itself repairs the sign qualification. Exactness is supplied by the usual bar contraction; freeness over \(A\) requires the stated base-module hypothesis.
fate: Pre-existing standard resolution, \citet[Ch.X]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard under the specified projectivity and sign convention.

title: Dual bar differential and its correct target
notes: The notes identify \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_s,A_0)\) with \((\bar A^*)^{\otimes s}\), insert reduced coproducts, and then write \(\operatorname{im}\bar\Delta\subset\overline{A^*}\).
statement: Under degreewise finite projectivity and graded duality, multiplication dualizes to \(\Delta:A^*\to A^*\widehat\otimes A^*\), and on the augmentation ideal \(\bar\Delta\alpha=\Delta\alpha-\alpha\otimes1-1\otimes\alpha\) takes values in \(\bar A^*\widehat\otimes\bar A^*\). The dual bar differential inserts this reduced coproduct with the bar signs. Without these finiteness conventions one must retain \(\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(\bar A^{\otimes s},A_0)\), rather than identify it with a tensor product of duals.
reconstruction: The tensor square missing in the target is visible as an error in both transcription and scan; the preceding diagram already has \(A^*\otimes A^*\). Completion or graded finite pieces resolve the infinite-dimensional duality.
fate: Classical dual bar construction; \citet[Ch.X]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct after the duality hypotheses and target correction.

title: Concatenation represents the Yoneda product
notes: The product of \([\alpha_1|\cdots|\alpha_s]\) and \([\alpha'_1|\cdots|\alpha'_{s'}]\) is the concatenated word.
statement: On the tensor cobar model, concatenate words. The differential is a derivation for this multiplication with respect to cohomological degree; hence it descends to cohomology and agrees with the Yoneda multiplication, subject to the choice of ordering convention in 1972-282.3.
reconstruction: In general concatenation is not commutative on cochains or on cohomology. This observation explains the method announced immediately above, without supplying its later classification theorem.
fate: Established bar-resolution product; \citet[Ch.XII]{maclane1963homology}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: The quadratic pencil and its separated eigenfunctions
notes: \(v^{\prime\prime}+2a\lambda v^{\prime}+b\lambda^2v=0\), \(v(0)=v(\pi)=0\), with \(a^2<b\), \(b>0\); \(v_k=e^{\gamma kx}\sin kx\), \(\gamma=-a/\sqrt{b-a^2}\), \(k=\pm1,\pm2,\ldots\). The associated PDE is \(u_{xx}+2au_{xt}+bu_{tt}=0\).
statement: Let \(a,b\in\mathbb R\), \(d=\sqrt{b-a^2}>0\), and let \(L(\lambda):H^2(0,\pi)\cap H^1_0(0,\pi)\to L^2(0,\pi)\) be the displayed pencil. Its nonzero characteristic values are \(\lambda_k=k/d\), with eigenfunctions \(v_k(x)=e^{-akx/d}\sin kx\), \(k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}\). The two signs describe the quadratic pencil; one-sign completeness is a different assertion.
reconstruction: The domain and the values \(\lambda_k\) are supplied. Direct substitution \ours after \(v=e^{-a\lambda x}w\) gives \(w^{\prime\prime}+d^2\lambda^2w=0\), independently checking both the sign and the scale.
fate: An exact normalized form and the distinction between the full and half root systems appear in \citet[section 1]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Completeness of the one-sided Kostyuchenko system
notes: The system is called complete. The final integral reformulation uses only the positive integers.
statement: For every real \(\gamma\), the linear span of \(\{e^{\gamma nx}\sin nx:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(L^2(0,\pi)\). The same statement holds for \(1\le p<\infty\). Consequently the signed system is complete, but its completeness does not imply minimality.
reconstruction: The half system is the precise object in the later entire-function question. The chronology of the original solution is verified indirectly through primary later research.
fate: \citet[section 1 and Theorem 1]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system} state the result and identify Kostyuchenko’s 1969 question and Levin’s 1971 function-theoretic proof. The later paper was received 15 February 1983 and published 1984. \citet[Introduction, pp.~509--510]{bilalov2012kostyuchenko} confirms this chronology. Levin’s original 1971 proof was not retrieved in this run.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the stated completeness problem was solved before the seminar. It is not a surviving open problem.

title: Biorthogonality requires the half system, not the signed list
notes: The coefficients are said to be unknown, but a biorthogonal system exists and is described using an inverse Schwarz--Christoffel integral.
statement: For the one-sided system and real \(\gamma\), completeness and minimality give a unique biorthogonal family \(w_n\in L^2(0,\pi)\), with \(\langle v_m,w_n\rangle=\delta_{mn}\), and uniquely determined formal coefficients \(c_n=\langle f,w_n\rangle\). The full signed system cannot have such a biorthogonal family: the positive subsystem is already complete and there are additional nonzero negative-index functions.
reconstruction: The one-sided correction is forced by completeness, rather than read into the signed display. The brief impossibility check is \ours: any vector biorthogonal to a negative-index element would be orthogonal to the complete positive family, hence zero. The independent check at \(\gamma=0\) gives the explicit duplicate relation \(v_{-n}=-v_n\).
fate: The one-sided minimality is explicitly reviewed in \citet[Introduction, p.~510]{bilalov2012kostyuchenko}, with references to the 1984--1985 work of Lyubarskii and Tkachenko. An exact matching Schwarz--Christoffel formula was not located. This is a partial identification of the asserted coefficient construction, not a claim that the 2012 paper contains that formula.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the half-system coefficient problem is developed in later literature; the notebook’s particular conformal-map formula remains unverified, and its signed interpretation is false.

title: The half system is not a Schauder basis when the tilt is nonzero
notes: \ru{Это не базис!}: not every vector has a convergent series expansion.
statement: If \(\gamma\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}\), \(\{e^{\gamma nx}\sin nx\}_{n\ge1}\) is complete and minimal but is not a Schauder basis of \(L^2(0,\pi)\). For \(\gamma=0\), it is the ordinary orthogonal sine basis. A signed enumeration is not a basis even at \(\gamma=0\), because it is not minimal.
reconstruction: The notebook assumptions allow \(a=0\), hence \(\gamma=0\). The missing hypothesis must be supplied if the assertion is about the half system.
fate: \citet[Theorem, p.~98, and Corollary, p.~99]{kritskov2015minimality} prove nonuniform minimality for a larger class, including this example under the substitution \(\alpha=-i\gamma\). The source cites Kritskov’s 1996 result for the unperturbed system. Thus the mathematical claim is established with the necessary nonzero-tilt qualification.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the zero-tilt half system is an explicit exception, not evidence of an unresolved basis question.

title: Analyticity of convergent expansions and an unspecified converse
notes: Every \(L^2\)-convergent expansion has an analytic limit satisfying infinitely many boundary conditions; the converse is asserted.
statement: For real \(\gamma\ne0\), convergence in \(L^2(0,\pi)\) of an ordinary series \[\sum_{n\ge1}c_n e^{\gamma nx}\sin nx\] implies that its limit has a holomorphic representative near every interior point of \((0,\pi)\). The same local conclusion holds for an ordinarily convergent series enumerating the signed system, since its individual summands tend to zero in norm. The notebook does not state the boundary identities or endpoint analyticity class needed for its converse, so that converse cannot be reconstructed uniquely.
reconstruction: Elementary necessity check \ours: convergence implies \(|c_n|\|v_n\|_2\) is bounded, while direct integration gives \(\|v_n\|_2^2=(e^{2\gamma n\pi}-1)/(4\gamma n(1+\gamma^2))\). Thus the series converges normally where \(\gamma\Re z+|\Im z|<\gamma\pi\) if \(\gamma>0\), and where \(\gamma\Re z+|\Im z|<0\) if \(\gamma<0\). These domains contain the open real interval, and normal convergence plus the original norm convergence identifies the limits. For a signed enumeration, the two coefficient bounds hold separately, so both half series converge normally on the intersection of their domains; no separate norm convergence of the halves is needed. The norm estimate was independently rederived by scaling at the endpoint where the exponential is largest; the two signs agree. This proves only the necessary interior analyticity assertion, not the unspecified converse.
fate: The later papers establish nonbasis behavior and analyze analytic function spaces, but the exact necessary-and-sufficient expansion theorem in this wording was not located. \citet[Theorems 5--6]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system} concern completeness in holomorphic/Smirnov spaces, which is not the asserted converse.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: interior analyticity has the elementary checked proof given here; the full converse and its boundary conditions remain an identification gap, not a defined open conjecture.

title: First-order Abel summation and the sign of the exponential
notes: The notes say first-order Abel summation fails and display \[\sum_{\lambda_k>0}c_ke^{\lambda_k t}v_k(x).\] The limit at \(t\to0\) is again said to be analytic.
statement: The usual decaying Abel factor for \(\lambda_k>0\) is \(e^{-\lambda_k t}\), \(t\downarrow0\); equivalently one may use the written sign with \(t\uparrow0\) from below. The manuscript does not specify this direction, the coefficient functionals or the convergence topology. Consequently no exact general Abel non-summability theorem can be extracted from the displayed formula alone.
reconstruction: The distinction between basis convergence and summability is essential. The sign is retained as a manuscript ambiguity; it is not silently corrected.
fate: The searched Kostyuchenko-system papers identify completeness and basis results, but no exact theorem matching this first-order summation assertion and its sign conventions was verified. Nonbasis behavior by itself does not imply failure of every Abel method.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the exact summation assertion is unverified because its definition and approach direction are missing.

title: Nonseparated boundary conditions
notes: For some nonseparated boundary conditions one can solve the problem.
statement: No particular boundary operators, parameter restrictions, solution space or asserted solvability result are supplied. The phrase can only be indexed as a proposed change from the separated Dirichlet model.
fate: Searches for the exact model and the later Kostyuchenko-system literature did not identify which nonseparated problem was meant. General operator-pencil solvability results are not an exact match.

title: Exponential sectorial growth of the resolvent
notes: The explanation of poor behavior is that the resolvent grows exponentially in sectors; a sector sketch is drawn.
statement: For the Dirichlet pencil above, the Green kernel is obtained by conjugating the Dirichlet kernel of \(d^2/dx^2+d^2\lambda^2\) by \(e^{-a\lambda x}\). Away from its poles, this introduces the factor \(e^{-a\lambda(x-y)}\), which explains why a nonselfadjoint exponential tilt can destroy estimates needed for contour summation. The manuscript does not give sector angles, pole separation or an operator norm bound.
reconstruction: The kernel conjugation is an elementary verification \ours from the displayed differential equation; it explains the mechanism without treating the drawing as a quantified estimate.
fate: The pencil is exactly identified in \citet[section 1]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system}. An exact asymptotic resolvent estimate corresponding to the notebook sketch was not located.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the elementary conjugation is explicit; the claimed sectorial asymptotic remains insufficiently specified.

title: Shortening the interval and excess completeness
notes: The system is overdetermined on \([0,\pi-\varepsilon]\).
statement: For the half system with real \(\gamma\ne0\), restriction to a shorter interval is expected here to mean excess completeness, rather than merely density; the notebook does not define whether deletion of one, finitely many, or arbitrarily many terms is intended. Density itself follows by extending an annihilating function by zero to \((0,\pi)\). At \(\gamma=0\), the Fourier-sine comparison supplies the familiar shorter-interval phenomenon.
reconstruction: The zero-extension check \ours proves only density. No exact deletion threshold is attributed to this sentence.
fate: \citet[Theorems 2 and 5]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system} distinguish completeness on subsets from completeness after deletion in holomorphic spaces. They are relevant but do not license identifying all meanings of the notebook word overdetermined.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: completeness on every shorter interval follows from the known theorem; the intended quantitative excess is unidentified.

title: Bernstein intervention on extending the completeness interval
notes: I. Bernstein says the system remains complete on \([0,\pi+\varepsilon]\), \(0<\varepsilon<\pi\); at \([0,2\pi]\) many orthogonal functions occur.
statement: The printed upper bound is \(2\pi\), but no distinction between the signed system and either half is supplied. The assertion is false under the literal allowed choice \(\gamma=0\): on any \((0,L)\) with \(L>\pi\), choose a nonzero function supported on a small pair of intervals symmetric about \(\pi\), with equal reflected values. Then its integral against every \(\sin nx\) is zero. A nonzero-tilt, specified-index version would need a separate theorem.
reconstruction: The counterexample is an elementary check \ours: \(\sin(n(\pi+s))=-\sin(n(\pi-s))\), so paired integrals cancel. Rechecking with \(n=1\) and \(n=2\) confirms the sign, and the identity proves it for all integers. This refutes the unrestricted statement but does not decide the intended \(\gamma\ne0\) version.
fate: The geometry-dependent completeness results of \citet[Theorems 2--4]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system} were read, but they do not state this exact real-interval threshold. No verified exact publication for Bernstein’s intervention was found.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal statement is refuted by an allowed parameter value; the intended nonzero-tilt threshold is an identification gap.
speaker: I. N. Bernstein

title: Completeness as an entire-transform uniqueness problem
notes: \(F(\lambda)=\int_0^\pi f(x)e^{\gamma\lambda x}\sin(\lambda x)\,dx\) is entire of exponential type and vanishes at all positive integers. The type and indicator work on a shorter interval; one must use the special form of \(F\).
statement: For \(f\in L^2(0,\pi)\) and real \(\gamma\), the displayed transform is entire and obeys \(|F(\lambda)|\le\sqrt\pi\|f\|_2\exp(\pi\max\{0,\gamma\Re\lambda+|\Im\lambda|\})\). The completeness theorem is equivalent to: if \(F(n)=0\) for all \(n\ge1\), then \(f=0\) almost everywhere. Entire functions of an exponential-type bound alone need not obey this uniqueness conclusion.
reconstruction: The explicit bound is an elementary estimate \ours: \(|\sin(\lambda x)|\le e^{|\Im\lambda|x}\), followed by Cauchy--Schwarz on \((0,\pi)\). The uniqueness conclusion uses the special integral-transform range, not an unrestricted Carlson-type assertion.
fate: \citet[section 1]{lyubarskiitkachenko1984system} identifies the function-theoretic proof as Levin 1971; \citet[Introduction]{bilalov2012kostyuchenko} independently confirms that this was the original problem formulation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: solved in the stated transform range; no unrestricted uniqueness theorem for all entire functions is asserted.

title: Replacing integer frequencies by a sequence
notes: \ru{Неизвестно, что будет, если заменить k на \(\lambda_k\).}
statement: The question asks when completeness/minimality survive for \[\{e^{\gamma\lambda_nx}\sin(\lambda_nx)\}_{n\ge1}.\] No allowed frequency class, separation, asymptotic density or perturbation norm is stated. There is no universal positive answer: repeated frequencies give a finite-dimensional span. A later sufficient-condition theorem must therefore be distinguished from an answer for all unspecified sequences.
reconstruction: No modern all-sequence classification is fabricated, and no residual open conjecture is assigned to a sentence without a specified sequence class.
fate: \citet[Theorems 1--5]{lyubarskii1985system}, received 14 May 1984 and published 1985, explicitly studies this replacement. For frequencies selected from zeros of a Fourier transform with analytic density, Theorem 1 gives completeness and minimality up to finite additions/deletions; Theorems 2--3 impose additional closeness or small-parameter conditions for the unmodified system. This is direct development of the question, but only a partial match to its unspecified scope.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: substantial precise perturbation results exist; the notebook does not define a remaining question with fixed hypotheses that could responsibly be classified C or D.

title: Function germs and the equivalence of hypersurfaces
notes: The notes start with \(f:(\mathbb R^n,0)\to(\mathbb R,0)\), \(f(0)=df(0)=0\), then specify that the actual setting is complex. Hypersurfaces are equivalent under changes of variables.
statement: The subsequent formulas concern holomorphic function germs \(f\in\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^n,0}\) with an isolated critical point, under right equivalence \(g=f\circ\phi\), where \(\phi\) is a local biholomorphism fixing the origin. Equivalence of reduced zero hypersurfaces is the weaker contact relation \(g=u(f\circ\phi)\) with \(u\) a unit; it should not be substituted into the Jacobian-algebra versality formula without adjustment.
reconstruction: The distinction between right and contact equivalence is supplied because the notebook alternates the words function and hypersurface.
fate: The function-germ convention is explicit in \citet[section 2]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Simple germs and the ADE list
notes: A simple hypersurface has only finitely many nearby jet orbits, uniformly in sufficiently high jet order. The \(A,D,E\) diagrams are drawn.
statement: A finitely determined holomorphic germ is right-simple if a sufficiently small neighborhood of a sufficiently high jet meets only finitely many right-equivalence classes. Up to adding nondegenerate quadratic forms, the simple isolated critical-point germs are \(A_k:x^{k+1}\) for \(k\ge1\), \(D_k:x^2y+y^{k-1}\) for \(k\ge4\), and \(E_6:x^3+y^4\), \(E_7:x^3+xy^3\), \(E_8:x^3+y^5\).
reconstruction: The whole list makes the diagrams explicit; the manuscript writes only the A-series normal form at this point.
fate: Exact prior source: \citet[Theorem 2.10 and section 7]{arnold1972normal}, received 21 June 1972, published in the fourth issue of 1972.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The first nonsimple stratum has codimension six
notes: \ru{Непростые коразмерности 6}; most orbits are called simple.
statement: In the space of sufficiently high jets with a critical point at the origin and critical value zero, nonsimple germs first occur in codimension six when at least three essential variables are allowed. In two variables the first such locus has codimension seven. This does not say that every nonsimple germ has codimension six, nor that every simple germ has codimension below six: \(E_7\) and \(E_8\) are simple examples of higher codimension.
reconstruction: The ambient stratum and the phrase first occur replace an otherwise ambiguous shorthand. Its codimension convention differs from the Milnor number.
fate: \citet[Introduction and Theorem 7.1]{arnold1972normal} states precisely these thresholds. Thus six is not a transcription error.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Versal deformation and its pullback property
notes: Every deformation \(G(x,\mu)\) is written \(F(X(x,\mu),\Psi(\mu))\), with \(X(y,0)=y\) and \(\Psi(0)=0\).
statement: A holomorphic unfolding \(F:(\mathbb C^n\times\mathbb C^r,0)\to\mathbb C\), \(F(x,0)=f(x)\), is right-versal if every holomorphic unfolding \(G(y,\mu)\) of \(f\) is induced by a holomorphic parameter map \(\Psi\) fixing zero and a parameter-dependent local biholomorphism \(X\) with \(X(y,0)=y\). The equality is one of function germs in both variables; the moving critical point need not remain the origin for nonzero parameters.
fate: Exact definition: \citet[Definition 8.1]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: A transverse slice produces a versal family
notes: Take the orbit and a submanifold transverse to it; a sketch illustrates the construction.
statement: For an isolated critical point, choose a sufficiently high jet order so that finite determinacy applies. A finite-dimensional family whose parameter tangent directions surject onto the quotient of function germs by the Jacobian ideal is infinitesimally right-versal and hence right-versal. An arbitrary transverse picture in an unspecified infinite-dimensional function space is not itself a proof.
reconstruction: The infinitesimal criterion and finite-determinacy setting supply the meaning of the geometric sketch.
fate: The operative implication is \citet[Theorem 8.3]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The Jacobian algebra and infinitesimal versality
notes: Every \(a(x)\) must be \(\sum_i(\partial_i f)h_i+\sum_jc_j\varphi_j\); the quotient by the Jacobian ideal is finite-dimensional, of dimension \(k\).
statement: For a holomorphic germ with an isolated critical point, \[Q_f=\mathcal O_{\mathbb C^n,0}/(\partial_1f,\ldots,\partial_nf)\] has finite dimension \(\mu\). An unfolding is infinitesimally right-versal precisely when the classes of \(\partial_{\lambda_j}F(x,0)\) span \(Q_f\) as a complex vector space. If these classes form a basis, the family is miniversal with \(\mu\) parameters. Finite dimensionality fails in general for nonisolated critical loci.
reconstruction: The notebook word generate means vector-space spanning in the quotient, not generation of the full local ring. The isolated-critical-point assumption is essential.
fate: Exact source: \citet[Definition 8.2, Theorem 8.3 and Corollary 8.4]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The Ak Jacobian algebra and miniversal unfolding
notes: For \(f=z_1^{k+1}+z_2^2+\cdots+z_n^2\), the derivatives are written without their numerical factors; the listed parameters multiply \(1,z_1,\ldots,z_1^{k-1}\).
statement: Over \(\mathbb C\), \(J_f=((k+1)z_1^k,2z_2,\ldots,2z_n)=(z_1^k,z_2,\ldots,z_n)\). Hence \(Q_f\simeq\mathbb C[z_1]/(z_1^k)\), and \(F=f+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\lambda_jz_1^j\) is a miniversal right-unfolding. The numerical derivative factors may be omitted from ideal generators, but not from equalities of derivatives.
reconstruction: The ambiguous early subscripts are normalized to 1 using the Jacobian quotient and the later displayed family; the scan itself retains i-like marks.
fate: This is \citet[Corollary 8.4, A-series]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The discriminant and its generic Morse points
notes: The bifurcation diagram consists of parameters for which singular points remain; on an open set of the diagram the singularities are called Morse.
statement: For a sufficiently small representative of a miniversal unfolding of an isolated critical point, its discriminant is \(\Delta=\{\lambda:\exists x,\ F(x,\lambda)=0,\ d_xF(x,\lambda)=0\}\). A generic smooth point of \(\Delta\) corresponds to one nondegenerate critical point at critical value zero. Thus the generic singular zero fibre has type \(A_1\); off \(\Delta\) the zero fibre is smooth.
reconstruction: Generic smooth stratum replaces the unspecified open set. The word simple here means Morse, which is narrower than the ADE notion of a simple germ.
fate: The definition and ADE discriminants appear in \citet[section 9, opening paragraph]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The polynomial discriminant and the swallowtail name
notes: For \(z_1^{k+1}+z_2^2\), singularity means \(P(z_1)=P^{\prime}(z_1)=0\); the diagram is called a swallowtail.
statement: For \(P(t)=t^{k+1}+\lambda_{k-1}t^{k-1}+\cdots+\lambda_0\), the zero fibre \(P(z_1)+z_2^2=0\) is singular exactly when \(P\) has a multiple root, so \(\Delta\) is its discriminant hypersurface. The ordinary swallowtail is the \(A_3\) discriminant; general \(A_k\) gives the corresponding higher discriminant, also called a generalized swallowtail in Arnold’s terminology.
reconstruction: The general label is not treated as a false formula; its special conventional meaning is clarified.
fate: The qualification generalized and the special \(A_3\) case are explicit in \citet[section 9]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The discriminant complement has the corresponding Artin group
notes: The fundamental group of the complement of the bifurcation diagram is the braid group of a Coxeter group.
statement: For a simple ADE germ, the complement of its miniversal discriminant is identified with the regular orbit space \(\mathfrak h_{\mathbb C}^{\mathrm{reg}}/W\). Its fundamental group is the Artin group of that ADE Coxeter system: adjacent generators satisfy the braid relation of length three and nonadjacent generators commute. For \(A_k\) this is the ordinary braid group \(B_{k+1}\), not the finite Weyl group itself.
reconstruction: The ADE restriction is necessary. The notebook does not assert this identification for all isolated singularities.
fate: \citet[Proposition 9.3]{arnold1972normal} gives the singularity identification; \citet[theorem, original pp.~57--58; Russian translation pp.~147--148]{brieskorn1971fundamental} gives the presentation. The original publication is 1971; the opened full text is its 1975 Russian translation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The Milnor fibre is a bouquet of middle-dimensional spheres
notes: A small nonsingular deformed fibre has homology only in degree \(n-1\) and is a bouquet of \(\mu\) spheres.
statement: Let \(f:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)\), \(n\ge2\), be holomorphic with an isolated critical point. For Milnor radii \(0<|\delta|\ll\varepsilon\), \(F_\delta=f^{-1}(\delta)\cap B_\varepsilon\) has the homotopy type of \(\bigvee_\mu S^{n-1}\), with \(\mu=\dim_{\mathbb C}Q_f\). Thus reduced integral homology vanishes outside degree \(n-1\), where it is \(\mathbb Z^\mu\); ordinary \(H_0\) is also nonzero.
reconstruction: The word reduced repairs the homology sentence. Smallness and transversality are required; an arbitrary regular fibre in an arbitrary ball need not have this type.
fate: \citet[Theorems 6.5 and 7.2, Appendix B, Problem 3]{milnor1968singular} proves the general assertion; the ADE case is \citet[Proposition 9.4]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Intersection form and the sign of vanishing cycles
notes: For \(n-1\equiv2\pmod4\), vanishing cycles satisfy \(e_i^2=-2\); negative definite, semidefinite and indefinite possibilities are listed.
statement: On \(H_{n-1}(F_\delta;\mathbb Z)\), the middle intersection pairing is symmetric when \(n-1\) is even and skew-symmetric when it is odd. For an oriented vanishing sphere in complex dimension \(n-1\equiv2\pmod4\), the self-intersection is \(-2\). It is \(+2\) when \(n-1\equiv0\pmod4\). Definite, degenerate and indefinite forms all occur among isolated hypersurface singularities; ADE gives the negative Cartan lattice in the stated congruence.
reconstruction: The notebook uses cohomology notation for classes subsequently intersected; homology vanishing cycles are used here. The word always is restricted to the displayed congruence.
fate: The conventions and ADE cycles are explicit in \citet[Proposition 9.4]{arnold1972normal}; signatures beyond ADE are discussed in \citet[section 1]{arnold1973unimodal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Monodromy on the vanishing-cycle lattice
notes: Monodromy is described only as a representation of the fundamental group, followed by an unfinished target.
statement: The smooth family over a discriminant complement defines \(\rho:\pi_1(B\setminus\Delta,\lambda_0)\to\operatorname{Aut}(H_{n-1}(F_{\lambda_0};\mathbb Z))\), preserving the intersection pairing. For ADE and odd \(n\), Picard--Lefschetz transformations act as the corresponding root reflections, so this representation factors through the Weyl group.
reconstruction: The target and the ADE factorization are supplied from the explicitly identified source; the notebook itself breaks off after the word representation.
fate: \citet[Proposition 9.5]{arnold1972normal} states this precise ADE realization.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: A programme linking local asymptotics and global topology
notes: Gelfand asks how to remove derivatives from Singer’s calculations and study global topology while sitting at one point; explicit asymptotics for second-order equations and a future Shnirelman report on Maslov are proposed.
statement: This is a programme rather than a defined conjecture: no operator class, coefficient formula, equivalence relation or target estimate is stated. The bounded identifiable themes are local proofs of index formulas and semiclassical/asymptotic methods; the named future talk is not itself evidence of a theorem.
fate: No exact publication can be matched to the undefined request. The later APS intervention in record 296 is a thematic crosslink, not proof that this programme was completed in precisely the intended form.

title: Completed divided powers and continuous duality
notes: \(A\) is additively \(\Lambda[[X]]\), with \(X_nX_m=\binom{n+m}{n}X_{n+m}\). Its compact dual consists of functionals nonzero on only finitely many basis elements. The next page uses a hatted tensor-product symbol.
statement: Use the degree-completed divided-power algebra and its continuous dual over discrete \(\Lambda\). The dual is \(\Lambda[x]\), paired by \(\langle x^n,X_m\rangle=\delta_{nm}\). In characteristic \(p\), the completion is \(\widehat{\bigotimes}_{i\ge0}\Lambda[Y_i]/(Y_i^p)\) when \(\Lambda\) is an \(\mathbb F_p\)-algebra. Finite internal-degree computations may instead use the graded algebra.
reconstruction: This completion convention clarifies the ordinary product sign on P463. ``Compact'' is the notebook's term for finite-support continuous functionals; it does not mean an arbitrary algebraic dual.
fate: Standard duality used in the later method; \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, with the topology specified.

title: The binomial coproduct
notes: Pairing multiplication with \(x_n\) gives coefficients \(\binom ni\), and the notes set \(x_n=x^n\), obtaining \(\Delta x^n=(x\otimes1+1\otimes x)^n\).
statement: For the preceding duality, \(\langle\Delta x^n,X_i\otimes X_j\rangle=\binom{i+j}{i}\delta_{n,i+j}\); therefore \(\Delta x^n=\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni x^i\otimes x^{n-i}\). Its reduced coproduct omits the two endpoint terms.
reconstruction: The stray star on one \(x_j\) in the first expression is a notation slip: all factors belong to the same dual polynomial coalgebra. The subsequent complete formula removes the ambiguity.
fate: Standard binomial duality; \citet[Ch.X]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct, with one local notation correction.

title: Cobar cycles and boundaries recover the Lazard equation
notes: Expanding the two reduced coproducts produces six terms, cancels the two \(h(x,z)\) terms, and gives the boxed four-term Lazard relation and a short exact sequence.
statement: In internal degree \(n\), \(Z^{2,n}=\ker d_3^*\) consists of normalized homogeneous additive two-cocycles, \(B^{2,n}=\operatorname{im}d_2^*\) consists of \(c((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n)\), and \(0\to B^{2,n}\to Z^{2,n}\to\operatorname{Ext}_A^{2,n}(\Lambda,\Lambda)\to0\) holds in the graded or continuous divided-power category.
reconstruction: Unlike the ambiguous polynomial-module notation on P467, \(A\) now has the correct divided-power multiplication. The single \(d_3\) without a star in the expansion is a notation slip, since the domain and the adjacent formulas are cochains.
fate: Same cocycle calculation as \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3]{lazard1955formal}; the later homological approach is documented in \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the symmetric restriction remains a further step.

title: Recovering the integral calculation from fields
notes: Because the equation does not involve \(\Lambda\), the notes say it suffices to consider \(\mathbb F_p\)-modules and \(\mathbb Q\).
statement: In any fixed degree the integral coefficient-and-relation module is finitely generated. Its rational rank and its dimensions modulo every prime determine whether it is free of a specified rank, via the structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups. Base change of kernels or Ext is not automatic; the argument should be made on the finite relation presentation or with the appropriate universal-coefficient sequence.
reconstruction: This supplies the missing integral bridge. Merely observing that an equation has integral coefficients does not justify identifying its solutions over an arbitrary ring with a base change of a field solution space.
fate: Lazard's integral coefficient argument provides the target conclusion: \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3 and Theorem II]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: a valid proof strategy with the finite-presentation and torsion step supplied.

title: Ext of a truncated polynomial factor: the characteristic-two exception
notes: For every prime \(p\), the notes write \(H^*(A_i)=\Lambda_p(u_i)\otimes\mathbb F_p[v_i]\), \(|u_i|=(1,p^i)\), \(|v_i|=(2,p^{i+1})\), and list degree-two generators \(u_iu_j\) for \(i<j\) and \(v_k\).
statement: For \(A_i=k[t]/(t^p)\), \(k=\mathbb F_p\), \(|t|=p^i\), odd \(p\) gives \(\operatorname{Ext}_{A_i}(k,k)=\Lambda(u_i)\otimes k[v_i]\) in the displayed bidegrees. At \(p=2\) it is instead \(k[u_i]\), with \(v_i=u_i^2\), not an independent polynomial generator. Thus the listed vector-space basis in cohomological degree two can still be used if this identification is stated.
reconstruction: \ours\ For \(p=2\), the reduced augmentation ideal has square zero, so its one-generator tensor bar cochain algebra has zero differential; all powers of the degree-one class survive. This directly disproves the exterior factor. The odd-prime periodic resolution alternates multiplication by \(t\) and \(t^{p-1}\).
fate: The normalized bar construction supplies the correction; \citet[Ch.X]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the uniformly stated ring formula is false at two; the corrected ring calculation is standard.

title: An associative noncommutative one-dimensional formal group
notes: The emphatic example is \(F=x+y+axy^p\) over \(\mathbb F_p[a]/(a^2)\), and the text says one-dimensional noncommutative groups exist with torsion.
statement: For any prime \(p\), this series is a formal group law. Its associator is zero because \((y+z)^p=y^p+z^p\) and \(a^2=0\); its commutator is \(a(xy^p-yx^p)\ne0\). Therefore commutativity fails over this nonreduced torsion base.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The included script checks the associator symbolically modulo \((p,a^2)\) and independently by arithmetic in dual-number rings for \(p=2,3,5\). The general proof is the Frobenius identity just given. This is the speaker's own later correction to 1972-276.2, not an invented counterexample.
fate: The characteristic-two version was already given by \citet[\S~I, after Theorem I]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct; it requires nilpotents as well as torsion, so torsion alone is not asserted to force noncommutativity.

title: Cocycles and actual laws: the square-zero qualification
notes: After the example, the notes say ``There are as many of them as there are cycles.''
statement: If \(I\) is an ideal with \(I^2=0\), normalized \(I\)-valued additive two-cocycles correspond exactly to laws \(F=x+y+h\) whose nonlinear coefficients lie in \(I\): higher nonlinear compositions vanish. For unrestricted coefficients a first-order cocycle is only a candidate deformation; higher associativity obstructions must be solved. Modding out by coordinate changes also identifies cocycles differing by a coboundary.
reconstruction: The local square-zero context makes the sentence valid. Extending it to arbitrary full laws or to their isomorphism classes would be false. Lazard gives noncommutative truncated laws over a reduced field that cannot extend to full one-dimensional laws.
fate: The extension distinction is explicit in \citet[\S~II, Theorem III and the following remark]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid as an infinitesimal statement, not an unrestricted counting theorem.

title: Normalized binomial cocycles and one indecomposable per degree
notes: The \(v_k\) classes are linked to symmetric groups. The coefficients of \((x+y)^{p^{k+1}}-x^{p^{k+1}}-y^{p^{k+1}}\) are divisible by \(p\), and the bracketed formula divides by \(p\). The last mathematical line says there is one generator in every dimension.
statement: Write \(B_n=(x+y)^n-x^n-y^n\). Its coefficient gcd is \(d_n=p\) when \(n=p^r\), otherwise \(d_n=1\). The integral primitive polynomial \(C_n=B_n/d_n\) generates all symmetric normalized degree-\(n\) additive cocycles over any base. In the Lazard grading this yields one free indecomposable in degree \(n-1\), and the full polynomial-ring theorem follows with the generation argument.
reconstruction: The \(1/p\) normalization is actually present in the scan and in the transcription's diagram; it must not be reported as an omission. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), the unnormalized \(B_{p^r}\) is zero, whereas the reduction of the integral quotient need not be zero.
fate: Exact published theorem: \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3 and Theorem II]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established since 1955; the semester closes an exposition of this result.

title: Homotopy smoothings and their equivalence
notes: A smoothing is a smooth \(N^n\) with a homotopy equivalence \(f:N\to M\); two are equivalent when a diffeomorphism of source manifolds makes the triangle commute up to homotopy.
statement: The object is the marked smooth homotopy structure set \(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\): pairs \((N,f)\) modulo a diffeomorphism \(h:N_1\to N_2\) with \(f_2h\simeq f_1\). For an oriented target the marking determines the orientation of the source. This differs from a smoothing of a fixed topological manifold, where the comparison map is a homeomorphism.
reconstruction: The later notation \(hS\) on P481 and P488 makes the distinction explicit. For the surgery statements below we use closed connected manifolds of dimension at least six and fix a reference smooth or PL structure as appropriate.
fate: Definition and equivalence agree with \citet[pp.81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}, notes circulated 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; the earlier letter S is retained as historical notation.

title: Twenty-eight smooth homotopy seven-spheres
notes: The page attributes \(\operatorname{card}S'(S^7)=28\) to Milnor. The prime after S is visually present but not defined.
statement: The group \(\Theta_7\) of oriented smooth homotopy seven-spheres up to oriented diffeomorphism is cyclic of order 28. The corresponding marked structure set over \(S^7\) has28 elements. This is not an assertion that there are28 unoriented diffeomorphism classes after forgetting the marking and orientation.
reconstruction: The interpretation of the unexplained prime is supplied by the precise established theorem. The counting theorem is due to Kervaire and Milnor, rather than a new seminar computation.
fate: \citet{kervairemilnor1963spheres}; the statement \(\Theta_7=\mathbb Z/28\) is also explicit in \citet[\S13.3]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established since 1963.

title: Describe the homotopy structure set
notes: ``Description of \(S(M^n)\)—?'' The next paragraph says Sullivan solved the analogous PL formulation.
statement: For a fixed closed simply connected smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\), \(n\ge6\), describe the marked homotopy structure set. Surgery gives \([\Sigma M_+,G/O]\to L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\curvearrowright\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\to[M,G/O]\to L_n(\mathbb Z)\), with exactness in pointed sets and an action on fibres. An individual numerical classification additionally requires computing the normal-invariant set and the obstruction and action maps.
reconstruction: The high-dimensional closed simply connected scope is an editorial reconstruction justified by the continuation on P488. It is not a universal solution in every dimension or fundamental group. This occurrence continues the normal-data and surgery themes of 1968-171.10, 1968-171.15, and 1968-173.2; the older homotopy-torus problem is narrower and receives no reused problem ID here.
fate: The structural answer predates the lecture: \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}; modern precise action form in \citet[Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the specified structural classification is established; the notebook asks no concrete uncomputed manifold case.

title: PL homotopy structures and the standard sphere
notes: Replacing diffeomorphisms by PL homeomorphisms gives \(PL(M)\), and \(PL(S^n)=\{S^n\}\) is asserted for \(n\ge5\).
statement: For a fixed PL manifold, define \(\mathcal S^{PL}(M)\) by PL source manifolds marked by homotopy equivalences, modulo PL homeomorphisms over the target up to homotopy. A PL homotopy sphere of dimension \(n\ge5\) is PL homeomorphic to the standard sphere, so this marked structure set is a singleton.
reconstruction: The statement concerns combinatorial PL manifold structures. It is not a uniqueness assertion for arbitrary singular triangulations, nor a smooth Poincare theorem.
fate: Classical high-dimensional PL Poincare result used in \citet[pp.69--72,81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated PL high-dimensional setting.

title: Thom quotient and the bottom fibre sphere
notes: \(T_\xi=D(\xi)/S(\xi)\), and a fibre over a chosen point gives \(i:S^m\to T_\xi\) for an \(m\)-plane bundle.
statement: For a real vector bundle \(\xi\) over a finite CW complex, its Thom space is the quotient of its disk bundle by its sphere bundle. The compactified fibre over a basepoint embeds as \(S^m\). Adding a trivial line suspends the Thom space, so stable bundle statements correspond to stable maps of these spaces.
reconstruction: A fibre orientation specifies the sign of the degree of a restriction. The stable rank is allowed to increase; this matters for the next criterion.
fate: \citet[\S2]{atiyah1961thom}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Thom coreducibility characterizes J-triviality
notes: \(\xi\) is called J-trivial if a map \(\varphi:T_\xi\to S^m\) has \(\deg(\varphi i)=1\). Connectedness is used to dismiss dependence on the chosen point.
statement: For a stable vector bundle over a connected finite CW complex, \(J(\xi)=0\) exactly when, after sufficient stabilization, its Thom space admits a map to the bottom sphere restricting to degree one on a fibre. Equivalently its associated stable sphere fibration is fibre homotopy trivial. A degree-one restriction also forces orientability; connectedness alone does not make an unoriented sign choice canonical.
reconstruction: The stable qualification is already suggested by ``large dimension'' in the notes. The precise statement is stable coreducibility, not a claim that every unstable sphere bundle is linearly trivial.
fate: \citet[Proposition~2.8]{atiyah1961thom}, using \citet[Corollary~2]{dold1955fibre}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established before the lecture.

title: Kernel of J versus a normal invariant
notes: \(K_J(M)\) is defined as stable bundles that are J-trivial. The later sequence treats it as the object represented by the smooth normal-invariant space.
statement: Bare stable bundle classes form \(\ker(\widetilde{KO}(M)\to J(M))\). The standard normal-invariant set instead records pairs \((\xi,\varphi)\), where \(\varphi\) is a specified stable spherical trivialization, modulo the corresponding equivalence. These pairs are classified by \([M,G/O]\), with \(G/O\) the homotopy fibre of \(BO\to BG\). Forgetting \(\varphi\) maps onto the kernel but can identify distinct normal invariants.
reconstruction: This is an essential refinement, not a change of notation alone. P488 draws a trivialization but its prose still suppresses it. The homotopy fibre represents a chosen null-homotopy; the set-theoretic kernel of maps into BO and BG does not by itself retain that data.
fate: The pair is explicit in \citet[p.80]{sullivan1996triangulating}; see also \citet[Proposition~9.21]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the normal-invariant interpretation is established; the literal bare-bundle functor is insufficient for the asserted classification.

title: Atiyah normal-bundle difference
notes: Atiyah's theorem, referenced as Matematika10:5, yields \(S(M)\to K_J(M)\), described only as a difference.
statement: If \(f:N\to M\) is a homotopy equivalence of closed smooth manifolds and \(g\) is a homotopy inverse, then \(\xi=g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\) has trivial stable spherical fibration. Equivalently \(J(\tau_N)=J(f^*\tau_M)\). The associated structure normal invariant further includes the trivialization induced by the homotopy equivalence.
reconstruction: The precise difference formula is supplied by the later P481 and P488 occurrences. The Matematika pointer resolves exactly to the 1966 Russian translation of Atiyah's 1961 paper; Buchstaber was its translator.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an established homotopy-invariance theorem for the stable spherical normal data, not for the vector bundle itself.

title: The PL surgery classification and the periodic obstruction
notes: A crossed-out ``always'' is replaced by dimension congruences. The display injects \(PL(M)\) into \(K_{PLJ}(M)\) and lists cokernels \(\mathbb Z\) for \(n\equiv0\) and \(\mathbb Z/2\) for \(n\equiv2\pmod4\).
statement: For a closed simply connected PL manifold of dimension \(n\ge6\), the refined normal invariant gives an injection \(\mathcal S^{PL}(M)\to[M,G/PL]\), whose image is the zero fibre of the surgery obstruction \(\theta:[M,G/PL]\to L_n(\mathbb Z)\). Here \(L_n(\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\) for \(n\equiv0\), \(\mathbb Z/2\) for \(n\equiv2\), and zero for odd \(n\). Thus in odd dimensions the normal invariant is a bijection. The exactness is that of pointed sets; a group cokernel is not implied.
reconstruction: Compactness, absence of boundary, simple connectivity, stable trivialization data, and the dimension restriction are supplied. With boundary there are separate relative conventions; with nontrivial fundamental group the obstruction groups involve the group ring. A terminal group in an exact sequence is not automatically its cokernel.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3, p.82]{sullivan1996triangulating}, circulated 1967; compare \citet[\S13.1]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the qualified PL theorem is established; the notebook display is too compressed to support an unconditional group exact sequence.

title: Sullivan computation of the PL normal-invariant homotopy groups
notes: The notes say Sullivan computed the homotopy groups of the representing space for \(K_{PLJ}\), without writing the groups.
statement: For the refined classifying space \(G/PL\), the positive homotopy groups are abstractly \(\mathbb Z\) in degrees divisible by four, \(\mathbb Z/2\) in degrees congruent to two modulo four, and zero in odd degrees. In dimensions at least five these agree with the simply connected surgery groups through the surgery obstruction. The degree-four comparison has a special normalization and should not be inferred from that high-dimensional statement.
reconstruction: The group formula comes from the cited literature. It is not present on this notebook page, which gives only the attribution. Modern G/PL denotes the stable version of Sullivan's F/PL.
fate: \citet[pp.69--72,83--84]{sullivan1996triangulating}; the high-dimensional identification is also in \citet[Remark~13.25]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, including the need to distinguish the dimension-four comparison map.

title: Smooth normal invariants: a reconstructed all-degree computation programme
notes: Immediately after the PL calculation: ``For \(K_J(M^n)\) it has not been done. A sequence for \(S(M^n)\) exists too.''
statement: Under the intended refinement \(K_J\rightsquigarrow[M,G/O]\), the remaining program is to determine \(\pi_q(G/O)\) in all degrees. For \(q\ge2\), the fibration gives \(\pi_q(O)\xrightarrow{J}\pi_q^S\to\pi_q(G/O)\to\pi_{q-1}(O)\xrightarrow{J}\pi_{q-1}^S\). Finite-degree calculations therefore require stable stems, the J maps, and extension data.
reconstruction: The notes do not name G/O, specify a degree range, or formulate an explicit conjecture. The all-degree program is a cautious reconstruction of the comparison sentence; taken literally for the bare kernel functor, a representing-space problem is not specified. No new finite range is invented.
fate: The reduction and low-degree tables are established in \citet[\S9.2]{ranicki2002surgery}. Finite stable-stem progress continues, for example \citet[Theorem~1.1]{burklundisaksenxu2026synthetic} (preprint 2024, online 2025, volume 2026), computing particular 82nd and 83rd 2-primary stems, not all \(\pi_q(G/O)\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: many finite ranges are known; no complete all-degree numerical determination was located in the primary literature checked through the status date. The reconstructed all-degree computation programme remains unfinished; no specific finite unresolved group is asserted.
worth: A specific bounded range or extension question could justify research. The notebook supplies neither; attempting a wholesale new stable-stem computation would not be a sound chapter-sized development. We retain the exact-sequence reduction as annotation and claim no new theorem.

title: Homotopy structures distinguished from actual structures
notes: \(hS(M^n)\) means homotopy smoothings and \(ht(M^n)\) homotopy triangulations; the latter is said to be describable.
statement: These are the marked smooth and PL structure sets defined by homotopy equivalences, with source isomorphisms over the target up to homotopy. Actual smoothings or PL structures on a fixed topological manifold use homeomorphic comparison maps and require a separate equivalence convention.
reconstruction: The letter h supplies the qualification omitted in the initial P478 label. The notebook does not define every equivalence relation for actual, rather than homotopy, structures here.
fate: Matches \citet[pp.81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard notation with the distinction retained.

title: Hauptvermutung: homology index and dimensional hypotheses
notes: A homeomorphism of manifolds can be replaced by a PL homeomorphism when M is simply connected and has no2-torsion in \(H^3\). The scan clearly places3 above H.
statement: A verified pre-lecture version is: if \(h:L\to M\) is a homeomorphism of compact closed simply connected PL manifolds of dimension at least six and \(H_3(M;\mathbb Z)\) has no2-torsion, then h is homotopic to a PL homeomorphism. Equivalently the integral \(H^4(M;\mathbb Z)\) has no2-torsion. For manifolds with boundary the corresponding simple-connectivity assumptions on boundary components are needed.
reconstruction: Replace superscript \(H^3\) by subscript \(H_3\), or by \(H^4\).
