These are different groups; the correction follows from Sullivan's original theorem and the universal coefficient theorem. ``Replace'' means homotope the given map, not assert isotopy. The missing compactness and dimension hypotheses must also be supplied.
fate: \citet[Main Theorem]{sullivan1967hauptvermutung}; precise obstruction and corollary in \citet[Theorem H and Corollary~1, pp.93--94]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the corrected high-dimensional homotopy Hauptvermutung statement is established; the \(H^3\) sentence is not the published theorem.

title: The normal difference is independent of a marked representative
notes: For \(f:N\to M\), with homotopy inverse g, the notes form \(\tau_M+g^*\nu_N\), where \(\nu_N=-\tau_N\) stably, and ask as an exercise that equivalent smoothings induce isomorphic bundles.
statement: The virtual rank-zero class is \(\xi_f=[\tau_M]-g^*[\tau_N]\in\widetilde{KO}(M)\). If \(f_2h\simeq f_1\) for a diffeomorphism \(h:N_1\to N_2\), then \(g_2\simeq hg_1\), \(h^*\tau_{N_2}\cong\tau_{N_1}\), and \(\xi_{f_2}=\xi_{f_1}\). Homotopy inverses are themselves unique up to homotopy, so the construction is well defined.
reconstruction: \ours\ This is the complete solution of the stated elementary exercise, using pullback homotopy invariance. It proves equality of stable bundle classes; it does not by itself identify the chosen spherical trivializations in a normal invariant.
fate: Compatible with \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom} and the refined construction of \citet[pp.80--81]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the exercise is resolved under the stated stable interpretation.

title: J-triviality and proper fibrewise equivalence
notes: The resulting \(\xi\) is declared J-trivial, drawn as a proper homotopy equivalence \(\xi\to M\times\mathbb R^N\) over the identity of M.
statement: Atiyah's theorem makes the stable sphere bundle of \(\xi_f\) fibre homotopy trivial. In sufficiently large rank it may be represented by a proper fibrewise homotopy equivalence of the associated Euclidean bundles; compactifying the fibres gives a degree-one equivalence of sphere bundles. The proper and fibrewise qualifications are part of the data.
reconstruction: Ordinary homotopy equivalence of the uncompactified total spaces would be too weak: every vector-bundle total space retracts onto its base. The notebook's diagram and the word proper prevent that misreading.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom}; the proper-equivalence formulation is explicit in \citet[p.80]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established after stabilization.

title: Equivalence of the two J-triviality criteria
notes: A second definition asks for \(T(\xi)\to S^N\) restricting to a homotopy equivalence on the fibre sphere; equivalence is called Dold's theorem and an exercise.
statement: For a stable bundle over a connected finite CW complex, proper fibrewise triviality and the degree-one Thom coreduction criterion are equivalent after stabilization. Dold's fibrewise equivalence criterion supplies the step from a fibrewise map inducing homotopy equivalences to a fibre homotopy equivalence; Atiyah's stable cofibration argument supplies the Thom-space step.
reconstruction: This separates two ingredients hidden in the attribution. The exact cited Dold result is 1955, Corollary~2, identified in Atiyah's Proposition~2.8 proof; it is not the unrelated Dold--Thom infinite-symmetric-product theorem.
fate: \citet[Corollary~2, p.121]{dold1955fibre} and \citet[Proposition~2.8]{atiyah1961thom}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved before the lecture; not an unfinished research exercise.

title: Common invariant subspace for a commuting compact-containing family
notes: \ru{сем-во попарно комм.} operators on a Banach space contains a completely continuous \(A\ne0\); the family has a common nontrivial invariant subspace. The notes call this a generalization of Aronszajn--Smith.
statement: Let \(X\) be an infinite-dimensional complex Banach space and \(\mathcal R\subset\mathcal B(X)\) a pairwise commuting family containing a nonzero compact operator. There is a closed linear subspace \(M\), \(0\ne M\ne X\), invariant under every member of \(\mathcal R\). The published theorem gives a subspace invariant under the entire commutant of any nonzero compact operator; pairwise commutativity of that commutant is unnecessary.
reconstruction: Complex scalars, infinite dimension, boundedness and closedness are made explicit; the stronger published theorem is not attributed to the notebook.
fate: The exact proof and a stronger theorem occur in \citet[theorem, p.~55]{lomonosov1973invariant}; received 5 February, published 1973. This develops the compact-operator theme indexed earlier as 1964-50.3.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established. Neither the unrestricted Banach-space invariant-subspace problem nor the Hilbert-space problem is a question posed by this entry.

title: Extension of the argument to locally convex spaces
notes: \ru{Док-во проходит в случае ЛВП, короткое и простое.} No completeness or compactness convention is specified.
statement: A sufficient precise version replaces \(X\) by an infinite-dimensional complete Hausdorff complex locally convex space and uses a continuous linear compact operator \(K\ne0\), where compact means that some zero-neighbourhood has relatively compact image. A commuting family containing \(K\) has a common nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. One must use the locally convex fixed-point theorem and this neighbourhood notion of compactness, rather than merely mapping bounded sets to relatively compact sets.
reconstruction: The complete Hausdorff formulation and the neighbourhood definition are a sufficient editorial formulation; no claim is made for every possible meaning of compact on an arbitrary locally convex space.
fate: The extension to real or complex locally convex spaces is explicitly stated in \citet[p.~56, paragraph after the proof]{lomonosov1973invariant}. The publication also leaves the precise topological conventions implicit.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The compact-operator fixed-point argument has this precise sufficient extension. The unqualified notebook sentence requires these conventions.

title: A compact image separated from zero and the transitivity alternative
notes: Choose a closed unit ball \(S\) about \(x_0\) with \(\inf_{x\in S}\|Ax\|>1/2\), then use \(\overline{AS}\). The displayed recipe reads \(x_0=\|A\|x'_0\), \(\|x'_0\|=1\), \(Ax'_0\ne0\). Orbit closures \(\overline{\mathcal R y}\) are invariant.
statement: For nonzero bounded \(A\), take a unit vector \(u\) with \(Au\ne0\) and \(t>(\|A\|+1/2)/\|Au\|\). Then the closed unit ball about \(tu\) satisfies \(\|Ax\|\ge t\|Au\|-\|A\|>1/2\). Compactness makes \(K=\overline{AS}\) compact and disjoint from zero. For a unital operator algebra, if every nonzero orbit is dense, then each \(y\in K\) can be carried into the open unit ball about \(x_0\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The explicit valid choice of t repairs the notebook formula. Reversing the triangle inequality independently verifies the separation. It is an elementary editorial check, not a new invariant-subspace theorem.
fate: This is the opening reduction of \citet[p.~55]{lomonosov1973invariant}; the publication asserts existence of the ball without the notebook's incorrect scaling recipe.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The reduction is valid after correcting the scale. For a small-norm nonzero A, the printed recipe places zero in S and cannot work.

title: Finite covering, convex weights, and the Schauder fixed point
notes: Finitely many \(T_i\) cover \(\overline{AS}\) by \(\|T_i y-x_0\|<1\). With the drawn cutoff \(f(t)=\max(1-t,0)\), form \(\Phi(y)=\sum_i\alpha_i(y)T_i y\), and apply Schauder to \(\Phi A:S\to S\).
statement: Set \(\alpha_i(y)=f(\|T_i y-x_0\|)/\sum_j f(\|T_j y-x_0\|)\). The denominator is positive on \(K\); the weights are continuous, nonnegative and sum to one. Only vectors in the open ball have positive weights, so \(\Phi(K)\subset S\). The map \(\Phi A\) is continuous with relatively compact range, hence has a fixed point \(x\in S\), and \(x\ne0\) because \(0\notin S\).
reconstruction: The value f(0)=1 and the positivity of the denominator are supplied explicitly from the graph; the missing parenthesis in one weight is restored.
fate: The construction is reproduced in \citet[pp.~55--56, displayed fixed-point equation]{lomonosov1973invariant}. Its chronology is the same as item 1972-290.1.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established proof mechanism. The dependence of the weights on y is frozen at y=Ax only after obtaining the fixed point.

title: The spectral contradiction does not promise a finite-dimensional invariant subspace
notes: The compact operator \(T=\sum_i\alpha_iT_iA\) has eigenvalue 1; the notes infer an invariant subspace and immediately caution that a finite-dimensional one need not exist in general.
statement: Under the temporary assumption of transitivity and for the commuting algebra in the notebook, \(E=\ker(I-T)\) is nonzero and finite-dimensional, and commutation makes E invariant for that algebra. Since X is infinite-dimensional, E is proper, contradicting transitivity. The finite-dimensional E belongs to the contradiction argument. The final theorem only asserts some nonzero proper closed invariant subspace. An injective quasinilpotent compact operator, such as the Volterra operator on \(L^2[0,1]\), cannot have a nonzero finite-dimensional invariant subspace over \(\mathbb C\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The Volterra example is an explanatory check, not a claim that the speaker gave it: injectivity excludes eigenvalue zero, and quasinilpotence excludes every other eigenvalue; a nonzero finite-dimensional complex invariant subspace would supply an eigenvector. The distinction between the commuting notebook proof and the stronger published proof is explicit.
fate: Compare the contradiction at the end of \citet[p.~56]{lomonosov1973invariant}; the published noncommutative-commutant proof instead uses E to obtain an eigenvector of A.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The qualification is essential. Compactness of A does not imply a finite-dimensional common invariant subspace.

title: A nontrivial closed ideal from compact multiplication
notes: A commutative Banach algebra containing an element multiplication by which is completely continuous has a nontrivial ideal.
statement: Let B be an infinite-dimensional commutative complex Banach algebra. If some left multiplication \(L_a:b\mapsto ab\) is nonzero and compact, then the commuting family \(\{L_b:b\in B\}\) has a nonzero proper closed invariant subspace I. Commutativity makes I a closed two-sided ideal. The zero multiplier must be excluded from this direct application, and dimension one is an immediate exception to the unqualified statement.
reconstruction: Infinite dimension and a nonzero multiplier are sufficient hypotheses for the stated argument, not a claim that the notebook gave them.
fate: This is the direct multiplication-representation consequence of \citet[p.~55, theorem]{lomonosov1973invariant}. The separate algebraic corollary is recorded in the seminar rather than stated in that two-page article.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established under the stated hypotheses; the original unqualified formulation omits necessary exclusions.

title: The Leray integral representation on a convex domain
notes: The displayed boundary integral has denominator \(\langle\partial\rho(\zeta),\zeta-z\rangle^n\) and coefficient \((n-1)!/(2\pi i)^n\). It is described for bounded holomorphic functions.
statement: A sufficient classical setting is a bounded smoothly strictly convex domain \(D=\{\rho<0\}\subset\mathbb C^n\), with \(d\rho\ne0\) on the boundary and \(f\in\mathcal O(D)\cap C(\overline D)\). With the boundary orientation and the standard alternating form \(\omega'(w)=\sum_j(-1)^{j-1}w_j\,dw_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{dw_j}\cdots\wedge dw_n\), the notebook formula reproduces f inside D. An arbitrary bounded holomorphic f needs a boundary-limit or limiting-domain interpretation.
reconstruction: Smooth strict convexity and continuous boundary values are sufficient hypotheses supplied for an unambiguous classical integral.
fate: This is established integral-representation machinery predating the announcement; compare \citet[\S1, Theorem 1.1 and Lemma 2.1]{henkin1969integral}. Strict pseudoconvexity requires a suitably constructed supporting kernel, rather than the unmodified convex-domain denominator.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; no new existence problem is posed by this formula.

title: A compact localization error with a half-Hölder gain
notes: The operator \(f\mapsto f g-f_g\) is said to be completely continuous and to satisfy a Hölder condition of exponent \(1/2\), but the displayed definition of \(f_g\) does not show its dependence on f.
statement: A precise sufficient interpretation uses a smooth bounded strictly pseudoconvex domain, \(f\in A(D)=\mathcal O(D)\cap C(\overline D)\), and a fixed smooth cutoff g. Apply a bounded \(\overline\partial\)-solution operator T with a half-Hölder estimate to \(f\overline\partial g\), and put \(f_g=fg-T(f\overline\partial g)\). Then \(f_g\) is holomorphic and \(f\mapsto fg-f_g\) maps the unit ball of A(D) into a bounded subset of \(C^{0,1/2}(\overline D)\), hence is compact into \(C(\overline D)\).
reconstruction: The definition through a solution operator is editorial. The notes do not specify the cutoff regularity, source norm, or whether \(f_g\) denotes a projection of \(fg\).
fate: The localization and uniform-estimate method is already present in \citet[Theorem 1.2]{henkin1969integral} and \citet[\S1]{henkin1970integral}. The precise abbreviated operator in the notebook is only partially matched.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The reconstructed compactness statement is established; identifying the exact boundary operator from the abbreviation alone is not possible.

title: A strictly pseudoconvex domain as a convex-domain section
notes: A domain with strictly plurisubharmonic defining function is a closed submanifold of a strictly convex domain and meets its boundary transversely; the parenthesis reads \ru{следует из теор. Ока}.
statement: Let \(D\Subset\mathbb C^n\) have smooth strictly pseudoconvex boundary. There are a Stein neighbourhood U of \(\overline D\), chosen with \(\overline D\) holomorphically convex in U, a proper holomorphic embedding \(F:U\to\mathbb C^N\), and a bounded smoothly strongly convex domain \(\Omega\) such that \(F(D)=F(U)\cap\Omega\) is a closed complex submanifold of \(\Omega\), and \(F(U)\) meets \(\partial\Omega\) transversely. The target dimension may exceed n.
reconstruction: Embedding, enlarged ambient dimension, analytic submanifold, regular boundary, and transversality are made explicit. The notebook does not contain an Oka-theoretic proof.
fate: The precise result appears in \citet[Proposition 14, Russian p.~111]{henkinchirka1975boundary} (1975; English 1976, p.~668); the modern formulation is \citet[Theorem 1]{forstneric2026embedding}. Fornæss obtained the independent 1976 realization. Class A records Henkin's coauthorship of the subsequent account.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established convex embedding theorem; a generic closed subset of a convex domain would not suffice.

title: Bounded extension from a transverse analytic submanifold
notes: In point 2, \ru{выпис. продолж. с подмн-зия с оценками!} in the class of bounded functions.
statement: Let D be a bounded smooth strictly pseudoconvex domain and let M be the intersection of D with a closed complex submanifold defined in a neighbourhood of \(\overline D\), transverse to \(\partial D\). There is a bounded linear right inverse \(E:H^\infty(M)\to H^\infty(D)\) of restriction, with \(\|Ef\|_\infty\le C\|f\|_\infty\). It can be chosen to take \(A(M)\) into \(A(D)\).
fate: This is the main theorem of \citet[pp.~536--537]{henkin1972continuation}, received 8 December 1971 and published in the 1972 volume. Thus the imperative in the notebook records an announced construction or exposition, not an unaddressed 1973 open problem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established under the smoothness and transversality hypotheses; these must remain attached to the estimate.

title: The converse geometric implication
notes: The converse is said to hold: such a submanifold is a bounded domain of holomorphy.
statement: A closed complex submanifold of a Stein convex domain is Stein. If it extends smoothly across the ambient strongly convex boundary and is transverse to it, the restricted defining function is strictly plurisubharmonic and defines a strongly pseudoconvex domain in the submanifold. Calling it a domain in \(\mathbb C^n\) additionally presupposes the given parametrization or embedding of D.
reconstruction: The word analytic and the intrinsic meaning of domain of holomorphy are indispensable; an arbitrary smooth or closed subset is insufficient.
fate: This is the classical Stein/submanifold direction used in the setting of \citet{henkin1972continuation}; it does not require the later difficult convex embedding theorem in the other direction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established geometric implication, distinct from the forward embedding theorem.

title: The maximal ideal space of A(D)
notes: For functions analytic inside and continuous on the closure, the maximal ideal space equals the closure of the domain.
statement: For a bounded smoothly strictly pseudoconvex domain \(D\subset\mathbb C^n\), every nonzero multiplicative continuous functional on the unital uniform algebra \(A(D)\) is evaluation at one point of \(\overline D\); the resulting identification of maximal ideal space with \(\overline D\) is a homeomorphism.
fate: Already explicitly recorded in the introduction to \citet[p.~219]{ovrelid1971generators}, using uniform approximation by functions holomorphic near the closure. It is not the unrestricted corona problem for \(H^\infty(D)\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established for the continuous holomorphic algebra under the stated domain hypotheses.

title: The symplectic Poisson bracket
notes: For a symplectic manifold M with matrix \(\omega_{ik}\) and inverse \(\omega^{ik}\), \([f,g]=\sum\omega^{ik}\partial_i f\partial_k g\).
statement: On a smooth manifold equipped with a closed nondegenerate two-form \(\omega\), its inverse bivector defines \(\{f,g\}=\omega^{-1}(df,dg)\), with the sign fixed by that inverse convention. Closedness is the condition making the Jacobi identity hold. The notebook's complex-coordinate form suppresses the factor i needed for a real Kähler form.
fate: Classical symplectic geometry, restated as the starting data in \citet[\S1]{berezin1974quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established definition; a nondegenerate but nonclosed two-form is not sufficient.

title: Associative quantization and the correspondence principle
notes: A family of associative rings \(A_h\) of functions has \(f*_0g=fg\) and \(\partial_h(f*_hg-g*_hf)|_{h=0}=\{f,g\}\).
statement: A formal interpretation specifies an associative \(\mathbb C[[h]]\)-bilinear product \(f*g=fg+hC_1(f,g)+\cdots\) on a chosen function algebra, with \(C_1(f,g)-C_1(g,f)=\{f,g\}\). An analytic interpretation instead specifies admissible real h, symbol domains and a topology for the limit. Factors of i can be absorbed into h; a real Hermitian convention usually has \(ih\{f,g\}\). These are different existence problems.
reconstruction: Formal series are supplied as one exact interpretation, not substituted silently for Berezin’s analytic family.
fate: The quantization definition and examples were announced in \citet{berezin1973bounded} and developed in \citet[\S1]{berezin1974quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established framework. The displayed first-order condition alone neither ensures associativity at higher orders nor selects a unique quantization.

title: The optional constant unit
notes: Requirement 3: every \(A_h\) has a unit corresponding to \(f_0\equiv1\).
statement: The constant symbol 1 is required to satisfy \(1*_h f=f*_h1=f\) on the specified symbol algebra for every admissible h. Having some nonconstant unit is weaker than this normalization.
fate: Explicit quantization axiom in \citet[\S1]{berezin1974quantization}; the later question on P000486 concerns precisely this extra requirement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Well-defined normalization; see problem GP-1972-401 below.

title: Trace and symplectic volume
notes: Requirement 4: a trace on a distinguished set, with \(\operatorname{Sp}(f*g)=\operatorname{Sp}(g*f)\) and \(\operatorname{Sp}f=c\int f\,d\mu\).
statement: For \(\dim_{\mathbb R}M=2n\), the natural volume is \(\omega^n/n!\). A trace is a linear functional on a specified ideal of integrable or trace-class symbols, cyclic whenever both products lie in its domain. The scalar c may depend on h. It is not asserted that every bounded operator or arbitrary symbol has finite trace.
fate: The trace axiom is formulated in \citet[\S1]{berezin1974quantization}; the actual operator-symbol trace identities already appear in \citet[\S1, formulas (1.13)--(1.16)]{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the models with the indicated trace ideal; convergence is part of the assertion.

title: Naturality relative to a chosen category
notes: Quantization should be functorial for canonical diffeomorphisms, with the qualification ``some fixed category''. Two Kähler classes are named.
statement: For a specified group G of symplectic symmetries, one may require pullback to act by algebra automorphisms of each \(A_h\), compatibly with composition. This covariance requirement is precise once G, the symbol spaces, and equivalence of quantizations are fixed. The notebook does not claim a functor on all symplectic manifolds and all canonical transformations.
fate: This relative naturality is built into \citet[\S1 and \S3]{berezin1974quantization}. Earlier prequantization items 1969-178.3--4 and 1971-229.4 concern different constructions.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: A meaningful specified-category axiom; unrestricted functorial quantization is not established by this entry.

title: The Gaussian Fock product and its domain
notes: An integral of \(f_1(z,\bar v)f_2(v,\bar z)e^{-|z-v|^2/h}\) defines the product on entire real-analytic functions.
statement: For h>0 use \(d\nu_h(v)=(\pi h)^{-n}d^{2n}v\). On polynomial symbols the formula \((f*g)(z,\bar z)=\int f(z,\bar v)g(v,\bar z)e^{-|z-v|^2/h}d\nu_h(v)\) converges and is associative; it equals \(\sum_\alpha h^{|\alpha|}(\partial_{\bar z}^\alpha f)(\partial_z^\alpha g)/\alpha!\). Larger analytic classes require growth estimates. Entire real analyticity alone does not ensure integrability against a Gaussian.
reconstruction: Polynomial symbols give a sufficient closed algebra. The measure convention removes suppressed powers of pi; unrestricted entire functions are not admitted.
fate: The Fock symbol calculus predates the seminar and is treated in \citet{berezin1972symbols}; see also \citet[\S4]{berezin1974quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established on specified symbol classes, with the displayed bidifferential formula also meaningful formally.

title: The Fock representation must be complex linear
notes: The representation formula writes \(f(z,v)\overline{\varphi(v)}\), while its next anti-Wick formula has \(\varphi(v)\).
statement: On \(\mathcal F_h=\{\varphi\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C^n):\int|\varphi|^2e^{-|z|^2/h}d\nu_h<\infty\}\), the covariant-symbol kernel acts as \((A_f\varphi)(z)=\int f(z,\bar v)\varphi(v)e^{z\bar v/h-|v|^2/h}d\nu_h(v)\). Domain conditions are needed for unbounded polynomial operators. Conjugating \(\varphi\) would instead make the map antilinear.
reconstruction: The bar is moved from the input vector to the second kernel variable as a mathematical emendation.
fate: The corrected kernel is the reproducing-kernel realization in \citet{berezin1972symbols,berezin1974quantization}. The scan confirms that the misplaced bar is in the manuscript.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The corrected formula is standard; the literal displayed map is not the claimed linear representation.

title: Creation, annihilation, and the two orderings
notes: The notes give \(a=\partial_z\), \(a^*=z\), normal and antinormal orderings, and symbolic monomials with opposite placements of bars.
statement: On the polynomial core of \(\mathcal F_h\), put \(a=h\partial_z\) and \(a^*=z\); these are Hilbert adjoints after closure and \([a_j,a_k^*]=h\delta_{jk}\). The normally ordered \((a^*)^m a^n\) has covariant symbol \(z^m\bar z^n\). A contravariant monomial is quantized in the opposite order \(a^n(a^*)^m\). The derivative without h is the h=1 convention.
reconstruction: The stated h-dependent Gaussian determines the adjoint normalization; the notation a* cannot simultaneously mean its Hilbert adjoint with the unscaled derivative.
fate: These are the Wick/anti-Wick realizations developed before the talk in \citet{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established after fixing h and the symbol orientation.

title: Coherent states and covariant symbols
notes: \(e_{\bar v}(z)=e^{z\bar v/h}\); the quotient of matrix coefficients equals \(\operatorname{Sp}(\hat fP_{\bar v})\).
statement: Write \(e_v(z)=e^{z\bar v/h}\), \(k_v=e_v/\|e_v\|\), and \(P_v=|k_v\rangle\langle k_v|\). For a bounded operator A its covariant symbol is \(\sigma(A)(v)=\langle Ak_v,k_v\rangle=\operatorname{Tr}(AP_v)\). The same vector must occur in both slots and the denominator; the notebook alternates v and \(\bar v\) in the labels.
fate: This is the definition in \citet[\S1, formula (1.2)]{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established. Off-diagonal polarization of the symbol is an additional analytic step.

title: Boundedness duality for symbols
notes: Bounded A implies bounded Wick symbol; bounded anti-Wick symbol implies bounded A.
statement: For normalized coherent states, \(\|\sigma(A)\|_\infty\le\|A\|\). For a normalized resolution \(\int P_vd\nu_h(v)=I\), the weak integral \(T_a=\int a(v)P_vd\nu_h(v)\) satisfies \(\|T_a\|\le\|a\|_\infty\). The two arrows concern different symbol maps and are not inverse norm equivalences.
fate: These estimates are in \citet[\S1, formula (1.14) and the compression construction]{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; a bounded covariant symbol alone is not the stated boundedness criterion.

title: Compactness and decay in the Fock model
notes: Compact A implies f tends to zero; a contravariant symbol tending to zero gives a compact operator.
statement: In the Fock model, normalized \(k_v\) tends weakly to zero as \(|v|\to\infty\), so compact A has \(\sigma(A)(v)\to0\). If \(a\in C_0(\mathbb C^n)\), then \(T_a\) is compact: approximate a uniformly by compactly supported symbols, whose coherent-projector integrals are trace class. The assertion needs this geometry and cannot be carried unchanged to an arbitrary frame.
reconstruction: \ours\ The two-sentence compactness verification is editorial; no equivalence with arbitrary vanishing covariant symbols is asserted.
fate: This is the symbol-calculus compactness mechanism associated with \citet{berezin1972symbols}; the stated sufficient Fock hypotheses explain the shorthand.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in this setting; ``all theorems hold later on the page requires additional assumptions for this one.

title: Trace class and the two trace integrals
notes: ``Nuclearity (analog.)'' followed by equal integrals of Wick and anti-Wick symbols.
statement:
If A is trace class, its covariant symbol is integrable against the normalized frame measure and \(\operatorname{Tr}A=\int\sigma(A)d
u_h\). If \(a\in L^1(d
u_h)\), then \(T_a\) is trace class, \(\|T_a\|_1\le\|a\|_1\), and \(\operatorname{Tr}T_a=\int a\,d
u_h\). These sufficient statements do not say that integrability of an arbitrary covariant symbol implies trace class.
fate: Read in \citet[\S1, formulas (1.13)--(1.16)]{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established with trace-class and integrability assumptions made explicit.

title: Gaussian conversion and the Weyl midpoint
notes: The Wick symbol is the Gaussian convolution of the anti-Wick symbol; h/2 gives the Weyl symbol.
statement: For a Schwartz contravariant symbol a in the flat model, \(\sigma(T_a)=B_ha\), where \(B_ha(z)=\int a(v)e^{-|z-v|^2/h}d\nu_h(v)=e^{(h/4)\Delta_{\mathbb R^{2n}}}a(z)\). In the consistent Weyl convention the Weyl symbol of the same operator is \(e^{(h/8)\Delta}a\). These constants depend on the chosen real coordinates and h convention.
fate: The conversion formula is explicit in \citet[\S1, formula (1.12)]{berezin1972symbols}; the flat quantizations are compared in \citet[\S4 and \S7]{berezin1974quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established Gaussian/heat relation; inverse heat evolution is not bounded on arbitrary function spaces.

title: Gelfand’s Poincaré attribution
notes: The parenthetical says that these are Poincaré's symbols, without a title, formula, or date.
statement: No uniquely identifiable mathematical attribution follows. It could concern symmetric ordering or an earlier symbolic calculus, but the notebook supplies no discriminating reference.
fate: Searches of the Berezin 1972 and 1974 papers and their bibliographies did not identify the precise Poincaré source intended. The established Weyl conversion in the previous item does not verify this historical attribution.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Attribution unresolved; no research problem or priority conclusion is inferred.
speaker: I. M. Gelfand

title: Continuous Parseval frames and the missing norm weight
notes: An overcomplete system satisfies \(\|f\|^2=\int|\langle f,e_\alpha\rangle|^2d\alpha\), but the contravariant reconstruction is written \(A=\int\mathring A(\alpha)P_\alpha d\alpha\) with orthogonal projectors.
statement: For a measurable continuous Parseval frame, \(I=\int|e_\alpha\rangle\langle e_\alpha|d\alpha\) weakly. If \(P_\alpha\) is the orthogonal rank-one projector, the appropriate measure is \(d\nu=\|e_\alpha\|^2d\alpha\), omitting zero vectors. Then \(A=\int a(\alpha)P_\alpha d\nu\). In general a contravariant symbol need not exist for every A and need not be unique.
fate: The norm factor is explicitly present in \citet[\S1, formulas (1.1)--(1.3)]{berezin1972symbols}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established frame construction; normalization cannot be dropped when the vectors are not unit vectors.

title: Compression and the Fourier example
notes: Embed H into \(L^2(M)\), multiply by the contravariant symbol, and compress by the orthogonal projection. The next page names \(e^{i(p,x)}\) on bounded domains.
statement: For the frame analysis isometry \(V:H\to L^2(M,d\alpha)\), \(T_a=V^*M_aV\); on VH this is \(PM_aP\). For a bounded measurable \(\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n\), the restricted exponentials \((2\pi)^{-n/2}e^{ip\cdot x}\) form a continuous Parseval frame in \(L^2(\Omega)\) by Plancherel. Their normalization determines the projector measure.
fate: This is the multiplication-compression realization in \citet[\S1, formula (1.5)]{berezin1972symbols}; the Fourier example is a standard instance.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established; writing PMP as an operator on the full ambient space adds a zero block.

title: The convex trace inequalities
notes: For a convex function \(\varphi\), \(\int\varphi(A)\le\operatorname{Sp}\varphi(\hat A)\le\int\varphi(\mathring A)\). The lower bound is called Jensen's inequality; the upper one is written as a compression inequality.
statement:
For a normalized projector resolution, a self-adjoint A admitting a real contravariant symbol a, and a convex scalar function \(\varphi\), one has \(\int\varphi(\sigma(A))d
u\le\operatorname{Tr}\varphi(A)\le\int\varphi(a)d
u\) whenever the terms are finite (or in a consistent extended nonnegative sense). The compression trace is taken on PH; in infinite dimension one cannot include an infinite zero block with \(\varphi(0)
e0\). Scalar convexity suffices for this trace inequality, not for an operator inequality.
fate: This is \citet[\S2, Theorem 2]{berezin1972symbols}, published before the seminar.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established Berezin trace inequalities with the trace domain and frame measure specified.

title: The Bergman cross-ratio and weighted holomorphic space
notes: The kernel \(G_h\) has diagonal Bergman factors in the numerator, and the Hilbert-space weight is \(K(z,\bar z)^{+1/h}\).
statement: In a homogeneous bounded domain with admissible h and a consistent analytic power of K, use the weighted space with measure \(K(z,\bar z)^{-1/h}d\mu(z)\), where \(d\mu\) is invariant volume. The normalized overlap in the product is \[\left(\frac{K(z,\bar v)K(v,\bar z)}{K(z,\bar z)K(v,\bar v)}\right)^{1/h},\] with a normalization factor and the invariant integration measure. Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the base of this ratio by 1; its reciprocal has the wrong concentration behaviour.
reconstruction: Both sign changes are mathematical emendations: the scan confirms the positive weight and reciprocal ratio. The unspecified volume density is also supplied.
fate: The corrected ratios and negative weight are in \citet[\S2, especially (2.23), and \S5]{berezin1974quantization}; the short precursor is \citet{berezin1973bounded}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established homogeneous construction. The formulas do not define a quantization on all real-analytic functions of every domain.

title: A constant unit outside the homogeneous case
notes: A marginal question asks whether there exists a quantization also satisfying condition 3; an arbitrary scalar \(c_1(h)\) is written in \(c(h)=h^{-n}c_1(h)\).
statement: The supported analytic question is whether the proposed Bergman-kernel integral construction can be given nontrivial symbol algebras and a constant unit on a specified nonhomogeneous domain. The domain class, admissible h, convergence bounds and allowed changes of kernel are not fixed. A separately precise formal variant asks for a unital associative deformation product on a Kähler manifold.
reconstruction: The formal theorem is contextual comparison only. The missing analytic category prevents identification of one precisely formulated question of which that theorem would be a partial solution.
fate: \citet[\S2.8, p.~1133]{berezin1974quantization} explicitly retains an analytic obstruction even to nonzero algebras without his hypothesis A. \citet[\S4, Proposition 4.3]{reshetikhintakhtajan2000deformation} construct a normalized unital formal product on arbitrary Kähler manifolds. That result does not establish convergence of the notebook integral or scalar normalization on every nonhomogeneous domain.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The formal unital theorem is established, but the intended convergent analytic problem is not identifiable with precise quantifiers. This occurrence is not registered as an open problem.

title: Homogeneity fixes the normalization
notes: For a homogeneous domain condition 3 holds and fixes \(c_1(h)\); \(e_v(z)=K(z,\bar v)^{1/h}\) gives the coherent system.
statement: For a bounded homogeneous domain and the admissible positive parameters in Berezin's construction, the weighted reproducing kernel is a constant multiple of \(K^{1/h}\). Transitivity makes the diagonal normalization spatially constant. Choosing the reciprocal constant gives the reproducing identity and hence constant symbol 1 as the unit.
fate: This is the homogeneous-domain construction of \citet[\S5]{berezin1974quantization}, announced in \citet{berezin1973bounded}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established for admissible parameters; arbitrary positive h is not part of the statement.

title: The shorthand uniqueness assertion on symmetric domains
notes: If the domain is symmetric and its motions act by ring automorphisms, \ru{то только это} (only this).
statement: No fully quantified uniqueness theorem can be recovered from these words: the class of algebras, equivalence, irreducibility and admissible parameters are missing. The later paper formulates exhaustion of irreducible effective w*-quantizations on classical complex symmetric spaces as a conjecture, with the sphere case then proved.
fate: Compare \citet[Introduction, pp.~341--342]{berezin1975symmetric} and the restricted uniqueness discussion in \citet[\S7]{berezin1974quantization}. They prevent treating the notebook's blanket phrase as an established theorem. No exact current problem is extracted from unspecified hypotheses.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The precise intended uniqueness assertion is not identifiable; covariance alone is not enough to assert it.

title: Can the Bergman kernel vanish?
notes: One parenthesis says \(K(z,\bar v)\ne0\); later the general case is called unknown.
statement: For a bounded domain G the off-diagonal Bergman kernel can vanish. Every planar annulus \(r<|z|<1\), \(0<r<1\), has zeros. In contrast the disk and bounded homogeneous complete circular domains have zero-free kernels. Positivity of \(K(z,\bar z)\) on the diagonal is a different assertion.
reconstruction: The negative unrestricted answer is separated from valid zero-freeness in the model homogeneous domains.
fate: The annulus counterexamples are already from 1969 (Rosenthal and Skwarczyński); the precise statements and original references are checked in \citet[\S4, pp.~258--259]{boas2000luqikeng}. The original 1969 full texts were not accessible in this run, so the chronology rests on this author survey.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: The unrestricted question had a negative answer before this seminar. No broader classification problem is silently substituted.

title: Global polarization of covariant symbols
notes: Covariant symbols continue from the diagonal to all of \(G\times\bar G\).
statement: For a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space with nowhere-zero kernel \(K_h(z,\bar v)\), the covariant symbol of a bounded operator polarizes as its operator kernel divided by \(K_h\); it is holomorphic in z and antiholomorphic in v on the product. If the denominator has zeros, the quotient may have poles and the blanket global extension no longer follows.
fate: This is the symbol realization under the kernel hypotheses in \citet[\S2]{berezin1974quantization}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established in the zero-free homogeneous setting; related to the preceding kernel-zero question.

title: Compact Hermitian symmetric quantization
notes: A Kähler potential is exponentiated; at \(h=1/n\) a single-valued kernel exists and the Hilbert space is finite-dimensional with computable dimension.
statement: For an integral positive Kähler class on a compact classical Hermitian symmetric manifold, choose its positive holomorphic line bundle L. At integral tensor powers \(L^n\), the quantum space is \(H^0(M,L^n)\), finite-dimensional; local kernels glue as sections with transition factors, not generally as scalar functions on all of \(M\times\bar M\). The potential is local and \(g_{i\bar j}=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}\Phi\), not the inverse matrix. The relation h=1/n uses a fixed integral normalization.
reconstruction: The line-bundle formulation supplies the indispensable global gluing and integrality conditions.
fate: The compact classical symmetric cases and their parameter/dimension formulas are developed in \citet[compact-space part]{berezin1975symmetric}. The notebook announcement precedes that publication; it does not supply a global scalar potential.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established for the specified integral compact symmetric models. Arbitrary Kähler scaling does not automatically permit h=1/n.

title: The disk and its projective symmetry representation
notes: For the Lobachevsky plane the notebook writes \(K^{1/h}=(1-z\bar z)^{+2/h}\), followed by a projective representation of its automorphism group.
statement: On the unit disk the Bergman kernel is proportional to \((1-z\bar v)^{-2}\). With \(\beta=2/h>1\), the weighted holomorphic norm has density proportional to \((1-|z|^2)^{\beta-2}d^2z\) and reproducing kernel \((1-z\bar v)^{-\beta}\). The automorphism group acts projectively by weighted composition; a genuine representation can be taken on a suitable covering group. The positive exponent belongs to the reciprocal weight, not the reproducing kernel.
fate: The disk specializes the homogeneous-domain construction in \citet[\S5, Theorems 5.1--5.2]{berezin1974quantization}; parameters and symmetry are developed further in \citet{berezin1975symmetric}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: Established. The displayed sign must be corrected and the Hilbert-space parameter range specified.

title: Four structure notations
notes: The page lists \(S(M)\), \(hS(M)\), \(t(M)\), and \(ht(M)\), respectively smoothings, homotopy smoothings, triangulations, and homotopy triangulations.
statement: The h-prefixed objects are the marked structure sets of homotopy equivalences, in the smooth and PL categories. The unprefixed terms refer to actual structures compatible with the underlying topological manifold. No new equivalence definition for the unprefixed sets is supplied here; later arguments explicitly concern \(hS(M)\).
reconstruction: We do not equate concordance, isotopy, and abstract diffeomorphism classes of actual structures, since the notebook does not choose between those notions.
fate: The homotopy-structure definitions match \citet[pp.81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard for the h-prefixed objects; the unprefixed notation alone does not specify a classification problem.

title: The set Phi must retain a specified trivialization
notes: \(\Phi(M)\) is called the set, then group, of stable smooth J-trivial bundles. A proper equivalence \(\varphi:\xi\to M\times\mathbb R^N\) is drawn, with \(N=\dim\xi\).
statement: The surgery construction needs stable equivalence classes of pairs \((\xi,\varphi)\), not only bundles admitting some such \(\varphi\). This refined \(\Phi(M)\) is \([M,G/O]\), equivalently the normal-bordism set of degree-one smooth normal maps after fixing the reference manifold M.
reconstruction: The drawing contains the required trivialization but the prose does not explicitly include it in the equivalence relation. We retain this distinction, as in 1972-287.7. The rank N in this paragraph is unrelated to the source manifold denoted N below.
fate: \citet[p.80]{sullivan1996triangulating}; \citet[Propositions9.21,9.43]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard after the essential pair-data refinement.

title: Normal difference and its zero normalization
notes: For a homotopy equivalence \(\alpha:N\to M\) with inverse g, the class is \(g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\). The parenthesis mistakenly calls \(\nu_N\) the normal bundle of M. For the identity, the sum is trivial; for a homotopy equivalence, Atiyah--Dold supplies J-triviality.
statement: \(\nu_N\) is the stable normal bundle of the source N. Modulo a trivial summand, \(g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\) represents \(\tau_M-g^*\tau_N\), is zero for the identity structure, and has trivial stable spherical fibration for any homotopy-equivalence marking. Its refinement with the induced trivialization is the normal invariant.
reconstruction: The wrong base M in the explanatory parenthesis is legible in the scan and both transcriptions. Correcting it to N is necessary for the pullback by g even to have the stated domain.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the local source/target slip is corrected.

title: The simply connected surgery obstruction sequence
notes: Assuming \(\pi_1(M)=0\), the notes display \(hS(M)\to\Phi(M)\to P_n\), with \(P_n=0,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\) according to the dimension modulo four.
statement: For a closed simply connected smooth n-manifold with \(n\ge6\), \(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\xrightarrow\eta[M,G/O]\xrightarrow\theta L_n(\mathbb Z)\) is exact in the sense that \(\operatorname{im}\eta=\theta^{-1}(0)\). The group \(L_n(\mathbb Z)\) is zero in odd dimensions, \(\mathbb Z\) in dimension \(4k\), and \(\mathbb Z/2\) in dimension \(4k+2\). The smooth obstruction map need not be surjective or additive.
reconstruction: The missing dimensional/compactness assumptions and the normal-invariant interpretation are supplied. A vanishing obstruction means normal bordism to a homotopy equivalence, not that the particular transverse representative already is one.
fate: Pre-lecture surgery theory: \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}; precise modern statement \citet[Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the specified range.

title: Adding the reference normal bundle and passing to Thom spaces
notes:
The proper trivialization is summed with \(
u_M\), inducing \(T(\xi+
u_M)	o T(N+
u_M)\).
statement:
For an actual rank-r representative \(\xi\) and its fibrewise trivialization, summing with \(
u_M\) yields a proper equivalence to \(\varepsilon^r\oplus
u_M\), hence a Thom homotopy equivalence \(\varphi_0:T(\xi\oplus
u_M)\simeq\Sigma^rT(
u_M)\). In the notebook's N+ notation, N means a trivial bundle of that rank.
reconstruction: A homotopy inverse \(\sigma\) may be chosen. To keep dimensions consistent in the next construction, one suspends the Pontryagin--Thom collapse by r; alternatively one works throughout with virtual rank-zero Thom spectra.
fate: \citet[\S2]{atiyah1961thom}; the resulting normal-invariant construction is explicit in \citet[Proposition~9.43]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard once rank and suspension conventions are stated.

title: Pontryagin--Thom collapse of the reference embedding
notes: For \(M^n\subset\mathbb R^L\), a normal tube gives \(\lambda:S^L\to T(\nu_M)\), transverse to the zero section with preimage M.
statement: Embed the closed smooth manifold M in Euclidean space and identify a tubular neighbourhood with the normal disk bundle. Collapsing the complement of its interior to the Thom basepoint gives \(\lambda\); near the zero section it is smooth and transverse, and \(\lambda^{-1}(M)=M\). Its stable homotopy class is independent of the auxiliary embedding and tube in the appropriate normal-invariant formulation.
reconstruction: The zero section is an embedding into the Thom space; it is the collapse map that is transverse to that section, repairing the syntactic ambiguity in the second notebook sentence. This repeats the construction of 1968-171.13.
fate: \citet[Example~9.41 and Theorem~9.42]{ranicki2002surgery}; the underlying construction is classical Pontryagin--Thom theory.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established.

title: Transversality produces a degree-one normal map
notes: Compose the collapse with a homotopy inverse \(\sigma\), deform it transverse to M, and set \(M_1=(\widetilde{\sigma\lambda})^{-1}(M)\). The boxed identity identifies its normal bundle as a pullback of \(\xi+\nu_M\).
statement:
With the suspension convention of 1972-293.5, make \(\sigma\circ\Sigma^r\lambda:S^{L+r}	o T(\xi\oplus
u_M)\) transverse to the zero section. Its inverse image is a closed smooth n-manifold \(M_1\), and the restricted map \(f:M_1	o M\) has degree one with stable normal identification \(
u_{M_1}\cong f^*(\xi\oplus
u_M)\). This is a degree-one normal map representing the given normal invariant.
reconstruction: The degree-one property follows from the chosen fibre degree and Thom class; it is not written explicitly in the notebook but is indispensable for surgery. The equality is a stable bundle identification, not equality of unrelated ambient normal ranks.
fate: \citet[Theorem~9.42 and Proposition~9.43]{ranicki2002surgery}; earlier occurrences 1968-171.10 and 1968-171.13.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an established construction, not a new existence theorem.

title: How uniquely is the transverse manifold determined?
notes: The page asks how uniquely \(M_1\) is determined; the next page says all such manifolds are related by Morse surgeries, attributing the statement to Milnor--Kervaire.
statement: A fixed normal invariant determines a normal-bordism class of degree-one normal maps. Different transverse approximations and compatible Thom homotopies give a normal bordism; a handle decomposition of that bordism gives a finite sequence of surgeries compatible with the normal data. It does not determine the diffeomorphism type of \(M_1\), and equality of bare stable bundle classes is weaker than equality of normal invariants.
reconstruction: The exact theorem matching the notes is the normal-map bordism theorem, followed by the surgery/handle decomposition of a bordism. No unique Kervaire--Milnor theorem locator matching this entire compressed attribution was found, so that attribution remains only partial. The underlying questions were already present in 1968-171.15 and 1968-173.2--3.
fate: \citet[Proposition~9.43; \S4.3]{ranicki2002surgery} supplies the precise standard statement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: resolved at the level of normal bordism; finer structure-set ambiguity is the next item.

title: Can surgery produce a homotopy equivalence?
notes: ``Is there a manifold there homotopy equivalent to M?'' The group \(P_n\) is called the obstruction to surgery to such an equivalence, and exactness is asserted.
statement: For the simply connected closed degree-one normal map in the high-dimensional range, its normal-bordism class contains a homotopy equivalence exactly when its surgery obstruction vanishes in \(L_n(\mathbb Z)\). In dimension \(4k\), the obstruction is the signature defect divided by eight; in dimension \(4k+2\) it is the Arf invariant of the surgery kernel's quadratic form; in odd dimensions it vanishes.
reconstruction: The obstruction formulas are supplied from the literature to make \(P_n\) substantive. They apply to the normal-map problem and require preliminary surgeries below the middle dimension, not to an arbitrary continuous map or arbitrary manifold.
fate: \citet[Theorem~13.2 and Example~13.3]{ranicki2002surgery}, consolidating the pre-1973 Browder--Novikov--Sullivan--Wall theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; this is an exposition of the surgery criterion.

title: The missing left term and h-cobordisms among films
notes: The sequence begins with a question mark before \(hS(M)\). Two structures yield Thom maps \(\beta_1,\beta_2\); a homotopy F is called a film, and the final question asks whether h-cobordisms occur among these films.
statement: For \(n\ge6\), the missing ambiguity is the action of \(L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\) on the smooth structure set. Structures with the same normal invariant lie in one action orbit. A transverse Thom homotopy represents a normal bordism \(W\to M\times I\); it can be changed relative to its ends to an h-cobordism precisely when its relative surgery obstruction is zero. Different films can change that obstruction by the image of \([\Sigma M_+,G/O]\to L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\).
reconstruction: This is an action exact sequence, not an ordinary group kernel-cokernel sequence. In the simply connected dimension range an h-cobordism is a product, giving the required diffeomorphism over M up to homotopy. The notebook's endpoint diagram omits normal-map data; stable bundles alone do not justify existence of F. Its Thom targets also contain an unclear \(\widetilde\tau_M\)-like sign where the preceding construction uses \(\nu_M\). We use the stable normal bundle in this reconstruction, while retaining the source reading as an ambiguity rather than silently changing it. The attribution to Novikov's dissertation is compatible with the earlier 1968 normal-map entries but does not uniquely locate a dissertation proposition.
fate: The precise answer is \citet[Proposition~9.48 and Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}; the pre-lecture smooth sequence already occurs in \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the structural question is resolved by relative surgery; no concrete uncomputed example is specified.

title: Finite determinacy and the action on jets
notes: For \(f:(\mathbb C^n,0)\to(\mathbb C,0)\), the group of \(k\)-jets of diffeomorphisms acts on function jets; a sufficient jet means that later terms do not matter.
statement: A holomorphic germ \(f\) is right \(k\)-determined if every holomorphic germ \(g\) with \(j^kg=j^kf\) satisfies \(g=f\circ\phi\) for a local biholomorphism \(\phi\) fixing zero. An isolated critical point gives finite determinacy for some \(k\); no particular universal jet order is specified here.
reconstruction: Isolatedness, holomorphic coordinate changes and the existence rather than a prescribed value of k are made explicit.
fate: This is the finite-jet framework of \citet[sections 2--3]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Modality counts families of nearby orbits
notes: \(m\) is the number of moduli; zero modality means only finitely many possibilities after perturbing coefficients.
statement: For a sufficiently high jet of a finitely determined germ, its modality is the least \(m\) such that a neighborhood is covered by finitely many families of right-equivalence orbits depending on at most \(m\) parameters. It is a local orbit-family dimension, not the dimension of the miniversal base \(\mu\), nor simply the number of coefficients in a chosen polynomial.
fate: Exact definition: \citet[section 1]{arnold1973unimodal}, submitted 12 March 1973; the zero-modality case is already defined in \citet[section 2]{arnold1972normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Zero modality is exactly ADE
statement: The complete list of holomorphic isolated right-simple germs up to stable equivalence is the ADE list of 1972-284.2, with \(k\ge1\) for \(A_k\) and \(k\ge4\) for \(D_k\). Conversely each listed type has modality zero.
fate: Published before this talk in \citet[Theorem 2.10, Corollary 8.6]{arnold1972normal}; the 1973 announcement recalls it as the zero-modal case.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Stable equivalence and the inappropriate positivity condition
notes: Stable equivalence means adding nondegenerate quadratic forms; the next sentence says the quadratic form is positive definite.
statement: Two complex holomorphic germs are stably right-equivalent if, after adding nondegenerate complex quadratic forms in auxiliary variables, they become right-equivalent. Every nondegenerate complex quadratic form is equivalent to a sum of squares; positivity is not an intrinsic notion over \(\mathbb C\). For real germs the signature of the quadratic summand is relevant and need not be positive.
reconstruction: The handwritten positivity sentence is faithfully reproduced; its correct replacement depends on the coefficient field.
fate: \citet[section 1]{arnold1973unimodal} uses nondegenerate forms. The real signatures in \citet[Introduction, formula (1.1)]{arnold1972normal} also rule out a blanket positivity requirement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The unresolved sentence about analytic coordinate changes
notes: \ru{Аналит. ф-я с точн. до анал. зам. перем. однозн. опр. зам. перем.}
statement: The surviving line does not specify what determines what. If read as uniqueness of the analytic normalizing coordinate change, it is false: even a nondegenerate quadratic form has nontrivial linear symmetries. Finite determinacy concerns existence of an equivalence, not uniqueness of a coordinate map.
reconstruction: The tautological diplomatic reading is retained; replacing its final words by Taylor polynomial or another guessed object would go beyond the scan.
fate: The surrounding finite-determinacy and modality definitions identify the subject but not the missing assertion. No exact publication is assigned to this line.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the intended assertion remains unreadable at the level needed for a mathematical identification.

title: The local smooth level manifold
notes: \(f^{-1}(\varepsilon)\cap B_\delta\) is a manifold with boundary of even real dimension.
statement: For a holomorphic germ with isolated critical point and radii \(0<|\varepsilon|\ll\delta\), transverse intersection with the closed ball gives a compact smooth real \(2n-2\)-manifold with boundary, whose interior is a complex \((n-1)\)-manifold. Its diffeomorphism type is independent of admissible sufficiently small choices.
reconstruction: The required order of smallness and boundary transversality are supplied.
fate: The admissible radius/value construction is explicit in \citet[section 1.1]{tyurina1968topological}; see also \citet[sections 4--6]{milnor1968singular}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Tyurina’s definiteness criterion
notes: The middle-dimensional integral intersection form is negative definite exactly in the listed ADE cases when \(n\equiv3\pmod4\); otherwise add variables. The attribution reads \ru{теор. Тюрина}.
statement: After stabilization to \(n\equiv3\pmod4\), the Milnor intersection form of an isolated complex hypersurface critical point is negative definite precisely for the simple ADE types. In complex surface dimension two this is the equivalence between negative-definite smoothing intersection form and a rational double point. Other congruences require the appropriate suspension and sign convention.
reconstruction: The attribution is to Galina N. Tyurina. Russian Тюрина here is the genitive form and should not be normalized as the surname of a different male author.
fate: The original surface result is \citet[section 3, Lemma 3, together with Theorem 2]{tyurina1968topological}, received 13 May 1967, published 1968. \citet[section 4, Remarks 3--4]{arnold1973unimodal} explicitly attributes the elliptic/ADE classification to G. N. Tyurina and states it in stable form.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Milnor number, bouquet and local algebra
notes: The level manifold is a bouquet of \(\mu\) copies of \(S^{n-1}\), and \(\mu\) is the dimension of the local ring.
statement: The precise statement is 1972-284.11: the Milnor number is \[\mu=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O/(\partial f),\] not the dimension of the whole local ring \(\mathcal O\), which is infinite. This finite number is the rank of reduced middle homology and the number of spheres in the bouquet.
reconstruction: Local ring is read as the finite local algebra of the gradient mapping, consistently with record 284.
fate: \citet[Theorems 6.5 and 7.2, Appendix B, Problem 3]{milnor1968singular}; the terminology local ring of the gradient map is used by \citet[section 1]{arnold1973unimodal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The E6 intersection diagram
notes: An \(E_6\) graph is labelled \(-2\) at a vertex and \(1\) at an edge; the quadratic form is said to be given by the Dynkin diagram.
statement: In a suitable distinguished basis of the Milnor lattice of \(E_6\), stabilized to complex fibre dimension \(2\bmod4\), the Gram matrix has diagonal \(-2\), entry \(1\) for adjacent vertices, and entry \(0\) otherwise. It is the negative \(E_6\) Cartan matrix. The diagram depends on a basis; it is not an unlabelled invariant for arbitrary singularities.
reconstruction: An independent exact matrix check \oursComputed gives the positive E6 Cartan leading principal minors \(2,3,4,5,6,3\), confirming negative definiteness after changing sign; see the accompanying code and output. The identification of the singularity’s lattice is the cited published result.
fate: \citet[Proposition 9.4]{arnold1972normal} gives the ADE rule. An explicit basis transformation for \(E_6\) is \citet[section 6, Example 2]{gabrielov1973intersection}, received 29 January 1973 and published later that year.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The unimodal classification announcement
notes: For \(m=1\) there is also a long list; the first displayed example is \(x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3\).
statement: Up to stable right equivalence, the isolated holomorphic germs of modality one consist of the three-index \(T_{pqr}\) series, including its three parabolic cases, and fourteen exceptional one-parameter families. The latter are named \(E_{12},E_{13},E_{14},Z_{11},Z_{12},Z_{13},Q_{10},Q_{11},Q_{12},W_{12},W_{13},S_{11},S_{12},U_{12}\). The notebook does not list these fourteen normal forms.
reconstruction: The family names and organization are reconstructed from the exact publication; the unrecorded normal-form table is not passed off as notebook content.
fate: Exact announcement: \citet[sections 2--3]{arnold1973unimodal}, received 12 March 1973, published 1973. \citet[Introduction, section 1.4]{arnold1974normal} gives the organized T-series/fourteen-family formulation; received 28 September 1973, published 1974.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the stated unimodal classification is established. Its published scope is isolated holomorphic right-equivalence classes up to stabilization.

title: The cubic example is simple elliptic with a two-dimensional radical
notes: The first modality-one example is \(x_1^3+x_2^3+x_3^3\).
statement: The cubic \(f=x^3+y^3+z^3\) has \(\mu=8\), modality one and intersection-form inertia \((\mu_+,\mu_0,\mu_-)=(0,2,6)\). It belongs to the family \(x^3+y^3+z^3+a xyz\), with \(a^3\ne-27\) for an isolated critical point. Its Milnor lattice splits as a negative \(E_6\) lattice plus a rank-two zero form.
reconstruction: The modulus and its excluded discriminant value are supplied. The notebook example alone already shows why a blanket nullity-one assertion is unsafe; the exact corank is read in the original calculation.
fate: \citet[section 6, Example 4 and Proposition 5]{gabrielov1973intersection} gives the lattice and corank two. The paper records Milnor’s letter to Arnold of 31 October 1972 about the parabolic monodromy groups; Gabrielov’s manuscript was received 29 January 1973.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The signature implications need two separate corrections
notes: With \(\mu=\mu_++\mu_0+\mu_-\), the notebook appears to assert \(\mu_+\le1\Rightarrow m=1\), and explicitly writes \(\mu_+\le1\Rightarrow\mu_0=1\).
statement: Neither displayed implication is true as an unrestricted assertion. ADE forms have \(\mu_+=0\), \(\mu_0=0\), modality zero. The cubic in 1972-294.11 has \(\mu_+=0\), \(\mu_0=2\), modality one. The matching valid result in Arnold’s announcement is that the cases with \(\mu_+=1\) are the nonparabolic T-series; they have \(\mu_0=1\). This does not assert that every unimodal singularity has \(\mu_+\le1\).
reconstruction: The first inequality is marked doubtful in the diplomatic transcription, so its exact sign remains an ambiguity. The second \(\le1\) is clear in the scan and is a faithful mathematical error. No silent replacement of both inequalities by equalities is made.
fate: \citet[section 3, Corollary Zh]{arnold1973unimodal} gives the precise positive-index-one statement; \citet[Proposition 5]{gabrielov1973intersection} supplies the decisive cubic counterexample.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal implications are false; the correctly restricted positive-index-one classification is established.

title: The hyperbolic T-series and its missing restrictions
notes: Under \(\mu_+=1\), \(axyz+x^k+y^\ell+z^m\) is called the three-index series \(T_{k\ell m}\).
statement: For integers \(p,q,r\ge2\) with \(1/p+1/q+1/r<1\) and \(a\ne0\), the germ \(x^p+y^q+z^r+a xyz\) is of hyperbolic type \(T_{pqr}\), with \(\mu=p+q+r-1\), modality one and \((\mu_+,\mu_0)=(1,1)\) after the stated stabilization. Equality \(1/p+1/q+1/r=1\) gives the parabolic types \((3,3,3),(2,4,4),(2,3,6)\), with parameter values restricted to keep the critical point isolated, and with a different signature.
reconstruction: Exponent restrictions, the nonzero coefficient and the hyperbolic/parabolic distinction are supplied. The three integers label a series; they are not three continuous moduli.
fate: The T-series and inertia-one characterization are \citet[section 3]{arnold1973unimodal}; the reciprocal-sum split is explicit in \citet[section 1.4]{arnold1974normal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The finite reduced J-group
notes: \(K(X)/J\text{-equivalence}=J(X)\) is called a finite group.
statement: For a connected finite CW-complex \(X\), quotient the reduced real K-group \(\widetilde{KO}(X)\) by the subgroup of stably fibre-homotopy-trivial virtual bundles. The resulting reduced J-group is finite. The corresponding complex version uses underlying real sphere bundles. If unreduced K-theory and actual ranks are retained, the quotient also has a \(\mathbb Z\) rank summand and is not finite.
reconstruction: Finite CW type, reduction and stable equivalence are necessary to make the displayed finiteness assertion correct.
fate: \citet[section 1, p.~181]{adams1963groups} explicitly separates \(J(X)=\mathbb Z\oplus\widetilde J(X)\) and quotes Atiyah’s earlier finiteness theorem; received 29 May 1963 and published 1963.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Adams operations determined on line bundles
notes: \(\psi^k(\xi)=\xi^k\) for \(\dim\xi=1\), together with additivity, determines the operations.
statement: For complex topological K-theory on finite CW-complexes, \(\psi^k\) is the natural ring endomorphism satisfying \(\psi^k[L]=[L^{\otimes k}]\) on line bundles. Naturality, the splitting principle and additivity determine it on all classes. It preserves virtual rank and obeys \(\psi^k\psi^\ell=\psi^{k\ell}\). Its value on a higher-rank bundle is generally a virtual bundle, not a specified bundle of the same actual rank.
reconstruction: Naturality and the splitting principle are supplied; additivity on a single fixed K-group without these conditions would not give uniqueness.
fate: \citet[pp.~162--163]{sullivan1970geometric} states the operations and Newton-polynomial construction; \citet[p.~7]{sullivan1974genetics} gives the line-bundle characterization. Both explain the pre-existing operations.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Fibrewise degree one and J-equivalence
notes: J-equivalence is fibrewise homotopy equivalence; a proper bundle map is required to have degree 1 on every fibre.
statement: Two real vector bundles of equal rank are stably J-equivalent when their unit-sphere bundles become fibre-homotopy equivalent after adding trivial bundles. A continuous proper fibre-preserving map, of degree \(+1\) on the one-point compactification of each oriented vector-space fibre, supplies such a stable equivalence: those compactifications are the sphere bundles after one additional trivial summand. A linear isomorphism is not required.
reconstruction: Stabilization, equal dimensions and the relation between unit spheres and fibrewise one-point compactification distinguish the two versions of the notebook definition.
fate: \citet[section 1]{adams1963groups} defines the quotient through sphere bundles. The fibre-degree construction and its localization variant are used in \citet[section 2, Lemma 2.3]{quillen1971adams}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Recovering the J-quotient from K-theory and all Adams operations
notes: The group \(J(X)\) is determined by \(K(X)\) as a module over the operations.
statement: For finite CW-complexes, Adams’s algebraic lower and conjectural upper J-quotients of real K-theory agree; the Adams conjecture identifies this common quotient with the topological J-quotient. The algebraic construction uses the subgroup generated by suitable \(k^{e(k)}(\psi^k-1)y\) as \(k\) varies, with sufficiently large exponents. It is not the image of one prescribed operation for every fixed \(k\).
reconstruction: The precise algebraic relation is supplied from Adams. Rank reduction and real versus complex K-theory must be fixed before using the notebook shorthand.
fate: \citet[Theorem 1.1 and section 4, pp.~208--209]{adams1965groupsiii}, received 25 November 1963 and published 1965, proves equality of the algebraic quotients. \citet[Theorem 1.1]{quillen1971adams} supplies the remaining conjectural relation. \citet[pp.~8--9]{sullivan1974genetics} explains the resulting universality.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The purported reverse Adams formula is false for each arbitrary k
notes: For every J-trivial \(\xi\), and every \(k\), the notes assert \(\xi=k^N(\psi^k-1)y\), after a uniform \(N\) has been chosen.
statement: The assertion is false already in integral real K-theory. \ours\ Let \(z\) generate \(\widetilde{KO}(S^4)\cong\mathbb Z\), so \(\psi^kz=k^2z\). Let \(M\ge1\) be the finite order of \(J(z)\), choose a prime \(q\nmid M\), and set \(k=q+1\). Then \(Mz\) is J-trivial, but \(Mz=k^N(\psi^k-1)(mz)\) would require \(M=k^N(k^2-1)m\). The right side is divisible by \(q\) and the left side is not. This holds for every integer \(m\) and every \(N\ge0\), and still holds after inverting \(k\), since \(q\nmid k\). Thus the surviving universal quantifier in k is decisive.
reconstruction: The counterexample is our verification of the literal quantifiers. The sphere-operation formula is checked in Adams 1965, p.~207; it also follows by injective complexification and the degree-four Chern character. An independent complex check gives the same verdict: in \(\widetilde{KU}(S^2)=\mathbb Zx\), \(x=[L]-1\), one has \(x^2=0\), \(\psi^4x=4x\), and \(2x\) has trivial realification because \(\widetilde{KO}(S^2)=\mathbb Z/2\). Hence J-triviality of \(2x\) would force \(2=3\cdot4^Nm\), impossible even in \(\mathbb Z[1/4]\). Both arguments were independently checked; neither purports to refute a differently localized or differently quantified statement.
fate: The exact prior theorem is the varying-k subgroup statement of \citet[Theorem 1.1 and section 4]{adams1965groupsiii}, not the displayed single-image equality. Sullivan’s completed version instead says a J-trivial completed class is \(\eta-\sigma\eta\) for some Galois unit \(\sigma\); see \citet[p.~9, corollary]{sullivan1974genetics}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the displayed universal formula is refuted; Adams’s differently quantified algebraic theorem is established.

title: The Adams conjecture, already proved before this report
notes: The converse is called the Adams conjecture: for every finite complex, some \(N\) makes \(k^N(\psi^k-1)\xi\) J-trivial for all \(k\).
statement: For a finite CW-complex \(X\), \(x\in KO(X)\), and an integer \(k\ge2\), there is \(N\ge0\) with \(k^N J(\psi^k x-x)=0\). The analogous complex statement uses underlying real spherical fibrations. A common exponent depending only on \(X\) can be taken: the J-image is finite, and each displayed difference has order supported only on primes dividing \(k\); any \(N\) at least the largest prime-adic valuation of its group exponent kills all such differences.
reconstruction: Virtual K-classes, stable J-equivalence and nonnegative exponent are supplied. Uniformity in k follows from the finite J-group and does not repair the false reverse formula. The uniform-exponent deduction is a finite-group check \ours: if the exponent of J(X) is \(\prod_p p^{a_p}\), take \(N=\max_p a_p\); only p-components with \(p\mid k\) can remain. This was checked prime by prime, including k divisible by more than one prime.
fate: Sullivan’s proof circulated in \citet[Corollary 5.9 and pp.~165--166]{sullivan1970geometric}, June 1970. The independent proof \citet[Theorem 1.1]{quillen1971adams} was received 3 July 1970 and published 1971. The expanded Sullivan treatment was published in 1974, so it should not be dated as a new post-1973 solution.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved; the notebook uses the historical name conjecture for a theorem already available in 1970--1971.

title: Naturality gives classifying maps for the operations
notes: \(\psi^k(f^*\eta)=f^*\psi^k\eta\); thus the operation is specified on the universal bundle over \(BU(n)\). The equation \(\psi^k(1)=1\) permits compatible stabilization.
statement: On reduced complex K-theory the natural operation is represented by a map \(BU\to BU\). Its restriction to \(BU(n)\) classifies the virtual class \(\psi^k(\gamma_n)-n\). Compatibility with adding a trivial line follows from additivity and \(\psi^k[1]=[1]\). This yields a stable classifying map, not automatically a lift \(BU(n)\to BU(n)\) for each \(n\).
reconstruction: The rank-zero shift is needed because BU represents reduced K-theory; the unrestricted group is represented by Z times BU.
fate: The representing-space construction and the stable versus unstable distinction are explicit in \citet[pp.~161--164, Proposition 5.8]{sullivan1970geometric}. This repeats the established operation represented in 1971-259.2.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Filtered equivalences preserve the intrinsic spherical fibration
notes: If an operation \(A:BU\to BU\) preserves dimension, the notes say \(A\xi\sim_J\xi\); they also say that such operations do not occur.
statement: The valid sufficient condition is a compatible family of homotopy self-equivalences \(A_n:BU(n)\to BU(n)\), preserving the stabilization filtration. The universal spherical fibration is intrinsic to this filtration, so its stable fibre-homotopy type is fixed. Merely preserving rank, or merely having compatible self-maps, does not suffice: the operation sending a bundle to the trivial bundle of the same rank satisfies both weak descriptions and need not preserve its J-class. Identity and conjugation already refute a literal assertion that no such operations exist.
reconstruction: Automorphism rather than arbitrary map is the missing hypothesis. The parenthetical word orientations is not adopted as a definition: preservation of filtration and orientation of a sphere bundle are different data.
fate: \citet[p.~71, theorem and corollary]{sullivan1974genetics} explicitly requires filtered automorphisms. The earlier \citet[section 4, inertia lemma; Corollary 5.9]{sullivan1970geometric} uses filtered homotopy equivalences. Proposition 5.8 explains the actual obstruction to extending all integral Adams operations unstably.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The universal sphere bundle in the BU filtration
notes: The inclusion \(BU(n)\to BU(n+1)\) has spheres as fibres; \(U(n)\) acts on \(S^{2n-1}\).
statement: The unit-sphere bundle of the universal complex n-plane bundle has total space homotopy equivalent to \(BU(n-1)\), giving \(S^{2n-1}\to BU(n-1)\to BU(n)\). Equivalently the next stabilization has fibre \(S^{2n+1}\). These two indices should not be conflated. The unitary action is the standard action on the unit sphere in \(\mathbb C^n\).
reconstruction: The scan leaves the first exponent sign uncertain; mathematical context selects \(2n-1\) for \(U(n)\), while the separate stabilization fibre is correctly \(2n+1\).
fate: \citet[pp.~68--69]{sullivan1974genetics} uses precisely this identification; \citet[p.~166]{sullivan1970geometric} explains the analogous orthogonal filtration and the intrinsic-fibration argument.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: The stable spherical classifying space and the J-map
notes: \(B_F\) is labelled the classifying space of bundles with a homotopy sphere as fibre; J is a functor.
statement: Let \(G_m\) be the topological monoid of self-homotopy equivalences of \(S^{m-1}\). Its classifying space parametrizes spherical fibrations up to fibre-homotopy equivalence. Stabilizing by fibrewise join gives \(BG\), and associating a sphere bundle to a vector bundle gives the natural map \(BO\to BG\), or \(BU\to BG\) after realification, representing J. The notebook’s \(B_F\) is identified with this stable classifying space.
reconstruction: The stable model and monoid, not a Lie group of linear transformations, are specified. A homotopy-sphere fibre means a space with sphere homotopy type.
fate: \citet[section 1, p.~69]{quillen1971adams} specifies \(\operatorname{Sph}(X)=\mathop{\mathrm{colim}}_m[X,BG_m]\); \citet[section 4]{sullivan1974genetics} develops the localized and completed analogues.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Completed spheres and their self-equivalence monoids
notes: Sullivan replaces \(S^{2n-1}\) by \(\widehat S^{2n-1}\) and introduces a group \(G_n\), preserving fibrewise homotopy type.
statement: Finite or prime completion can be applied fibrewise to spherical fibrations. Fibrations with a completed-sphere fibre are classified by the classifying space of its homotopy self-equivalence monoid. The completed universal fibration over \(\widehat{BU(n)}\) pulls back to the fibrewise completion of the ordinary one. Completed and ordinary fibrations must be distinguished; after stabilization the oriented completed theory recovers the ordinary stable oriented spherical theory.
reconstruction: The manuscript does not define its \(G_n\). The homotopy self-equivalence monoid is a precise model supporting the displayed classifying-space argument, not a recovered literal definition.
fate: \citet[section 4, especially Corollary 4, pp.~65--66; p.~69]{sullivan1974genetics} gives this comparison. It was already part of \citet[section 4 and Corollary 5.9]{sullivan1970geometric}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established with the hypotheses and distinctions stated here.

title: Sullivan completion and its universal mapping property
notes: For simply connected complexes with finitely generated homotopy groups there is a functorial \(X\to\widehat X\), through which maps to spaces with finite homotopy groups factor.
statement: For a simply connected CW-complex whose homotopy groups are finitely generated, Sullivan finite completion gives a natural homotopy type \(\widehat X\). For a finite Postnikov target \(F\) with finite homotopy groups, precomposition gives a bijection \([\widehat X,F]\to[X,F]\); the more general formulation uses Sullivan’s compact homotopy functors. Uniqueness is up to homotopy, not uniqueness of a strict map between chosen point-set models.
